a44.speaker: Government of Mozambique and US Embassy (joint announcement)
a44.speech: Announced a $537 million financing agreement under the second Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact, funded by the United States, to be used for building climate-resilient infrastructure, coastal development, and strengthening local economies in Zambezia province that depend on agriculture and fishing.

a88.speaker: Christine Stegling, Deputy Executive Director of UNAIDS
a88.speech: "That's 20 million out of the 30 million people living with HIV in the world," said Christine Stegling at a scheduled press briefing in Geneva. Said what they're really concerned about is that governments will focus right now on keeping people on treatment rather than preventing new infections. Said "there is a lot of confusion on the ground especially at the community level on how the waiver will be implemented," pointing to disruption of treatment services. On Ethiopia, said: "All of these, in all regions of Ethiopia, have been terminated, as well as 10,000 data clerks, very important in Ethiopia." Said if PEPFAR is not re-authorized between 2025 and 2029 and other resources are not found, "there would be a 400 per cent increase in AIDS death... That's 6.3 million people, 6.3 million AIDS related deaths that will occur in the future."

a88.speaker: UNAIDS (organization)
a88.speech: Said transport services and community health workers are also still impacted by the US funding pause. Highlighted that the pause in US assistance to community programmes would lead to the closure of many drop-in health centres and the termination of outreach workers' contracts, depriving vulnerable groups of support. Said the biggest interruption will be to community health services, which have been crucial to the fight against HIV. Said it is most concerned about the long-term impact of the US funding freeze on prevention of new HIV infections. Said it will continue efforts to ensure that during the 90-day pause, all people affected by HIV continue to access life-saving services.

a125.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of Tahoua region
a125.speech: At an extraordinary meeting of the regional technical flood-management committee, drew up an alarming assessment of the situation: the floods affected more than 31,523 households, some 214,580 people, and caused the collapse of more than 23,523 houses; the human toll is also heavy with 104 deaths and 81 injured; the floods led to the loss of 10,028 head of livestock and the destruction of 154 hectares of cultivable land; the education sector suffered significant damage, with nearly 291 classrooms damaged and 274 other classrooms sheltering disaster-affected families, disrupting the schooling of thousands of children.

a125.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of Tahoua region
a125.speech: Praised the promptness and effectiveness of the relief interventions, stressing the importance of national and international solidarity in this ordeal, and congratulated the members of the regional technical committee for their hard work ; praised the responsiveness of humanitarian actors and called for the continuation of efforts to assist the disaster-affected populations, likewise underlining the importance of solidarity in facing this crisis and highlighting the need to prevent and prepare for natural disasters.

a242.speaker: Reuters (citing Ukrainian diplomats of various ranks)
a242.speech: Reports that Kyiv has sent humanitarian aid to Mauritania for refugees from neighbouring Mali, and has offered Nouakchott its assistance in training the Mauritanian armed forces, drawing on the combat experience acquired in its war against Russia.

a242.speaker: Maksym Subkh, Ukraine's Special Representative for the Middle East and Africa
a242.speech: "Ukraine is ready to continue training officers and members of the Mauritanian armed forces, and to share the technologies and achievements obtained [in its war against Russia]."

a242.speaker: Reuters' interlocutor (Ukrainian diplomatic source, anonymous)
a242.speech: Specified that Kyiv was already training Mauritanian soldiers before February 2022.

a242.speaker: Mauritanian authorities (non-response)
a242.speech: For now, the Mauritanian authorities have not commented on the possibility of resorting to Ukrainian assistance.

a242.speaker: Senenews (Senegalese media outlet)
a242.speech: Reports that the Malian authorities' investigation indicates that the fighters' training reportedly took place on Mauritanian territory, with the participation of Ukrainian instructors.

a242.speaker: Government of Mauritania
a242.speech: In response to a diplomatic request from Mali, affirmed that it was "not involved in the Malian conflict, nor supporting the Azawad movement," and launched an investigation to shed light on the events.

a242.speaker: Andriy Yusov, spokesman for Ukrainian intelligence, and Yuri Pivovarov, Ukraine's ambassador to Senegal
a242.speech: Spoke publicly about the alleged Ukrainian involvement in the July 2024 attack on a Malian army convoy in northern Mali.

a242.speaker: Ukrainian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a242.speech: Rejected the accusations made by Mali regarding participation in the attack on the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa).

a242.speaker: Bamako / Malian authorities
a242.speech: Say that a phone containing photos of Ukrainian services documents and a drone bearing Ukrainian inscriptions, found in a vehicle abandoned by jihadists, confirmed active cooperation between Kyiv and the terrorists of JNIM; and that it is through Mauritania that Ukrainian FPV-type drones transit to the region.

a242.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Malian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a242.speech: Described Ukraine as a "sponsor of terrorism" and called for Kyiv to be stopped ; "These terrorists (regional) are supported by external, regional actors who are in our neighbourhood, who back them, offer them a rear base. Ukraine, for example. [...] Ukraine is a sponsor of terrorism and must be stopped."

a242.speaker: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger (joint petition to the UN Security Council, 2024)
a242.speech: Petitioned the UN Security Council to request an investigation into the alleged links between Ukraine and terrorist groups in the Sahel.

a242.speaker: Ukrainian Embassy in Nouakchott
a242.speech: Announced in June that it had delivered 1,400 tonnes of humanitarian aid to the Mbera refugee camp, the largest in West Africa, which hosts some 250,000 people, in three stages within the framework of the UN World Food Programme (WFP).

a242.speaker: Reuters
a242.speech: Stresses that the volume of humanitarian aid that reached Sahelian refugees has remained "limited" ; highlights the weakness of the human and logistical resources of Ukrainian diplomatic missions in Africa ; "Kyiv cannot compete with its adversary (Russia), which has deep ties in the fields of economic cooperation and security [...]. Russia has around 40 diplomatic representations on the African continent, and it recently announced the forthcoming opening of seven more."

a242.speaker: Mauritanian Ministry of Communication
a242.speech: Said it could not confirm the arrival of the cargo at the camp.

a242.speaker: Viktor Bort, Ukrainian diplomat, head of the diplomatic mission in Nouakchott since 2024
a242.speech: Specified that the products delivered to the Africans included chickpeas, vegetable oil and wheat ; acknowledged having been given the mission of establishing ties with the Mauritanian authorities and of supervising deliveries of aid intended for Malian refugees, recognising the political stakes of the deliveries.

a242.speaker: Maksym Subkh, Ukraine's Special Representative for the Middle East and Africa
a242.speech: Stated that decisions concerning the distribution of aid were a matter for the World Food Programme (WFP), and that Ukraine opposed any "politicisation of humanitarian aid."

a242.speaker: Roman Sereda, Ukrainian ambassador in Nouakchott
a242.speech: Contradicted Mr Subkh by asserting that Ukraine intended to prevent Russia from "using food as political leverage," and hoped to convince African countries to pressure Moscow to end the special operation ; specified that the humanitarian deliveries to Mauritania were accompanied by an "information campaign" which, according to him, had "improved Kyiv's image."

a445.speaker: Sheikh Dr. Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais, President of Religious Affairs at the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque
a445.speech: Stressed in his speech at the plan's launch ceremony that the wise leadership - may God protect it - has employed all of its capabilities to serve the guests of God through digital transformation tools and artificial intelligence, to provide them with a unique faith experience and to enrich the pilgrims' experience of faith, contributing to reducing the barriers of time and place and to delivering the moderate and humane message of Hajj to the whole world in various languages.

a445.speaker: Sheikh Dr. Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais, President of Religious Affairs at the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque
a445.speech: Said that the operational plan for the 1446 Hajj season focuses on digital and smart transformation projects and on addressing the guests of God and of the world in multiple languages, reflecting the Religious Presidency's commitment to keeping pace with the national vision for digital transformation and leadership in technology, smart technologies and artificial robotics ; noted that the moderate message of the 1446 Hajj season will be highlighted through interactive, smart, digital and multilingual platforms that reflect the objectives of Sharia and promote moderate and balanced Islamic values.

a445.speaker: Sheikh Dr. Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais, President of Religious Affairs at the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque
a445.speech: Noted that emphasis is being placed on serving the pilgrims, enriching the experience of the guests of God and implementing distinguished scientific, intellectual and advisory initiatives, which constitutes a main pillar of the operational plan, promoting the values of moderation, tolerance and balance while deepening the dimensions of the pilgrims' journey of faith through faith-based programmes of global impact and benefit.

a778.speaker: Libuseng Mokhoang, 21-year-old founder of Botanica Range, winner in the Manufacturing (Consumables) category
a778.speech: "I am truly grateful and thankful for the support that I got."

a778.speaker: 'Mamashiya Ntsepeng Tsita Tikiso, President of the BAM Group Foundation
a778.speech: Praised the nominees and explained the event's mission: "We brought you together because we want to work hard on women empowerment; we want to see every woman progress." ; "We want to see every woman envision herself as strong, empowered, and know that they have the possibility to reach their goals."

a778.speaker: 'Mamashiya Ntsepeng Tsita Tikiso, President of the BAM Group Foundation
a778.speech: Emphasised that every nominee was already a winner: "The fact that you have been nominated says a lot about your competence. Somebody showed up for you by nominating you," encouraging those not nominated to "work hard in your sphere because we would like to recognise you."

a778.speaker: Pitso Lesaoana, Minister of Gender of Lesotho
a778.speech: In his closing remarks, applauded the fearless and courageous spirit of the women honoured: "Ladies, for all the great things you have done, you have proven beyond doubt that you are not inferior but equals, especially when it comes to business."

a934.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a934.speech: Has urged Namibian businesses to explore opportunities in e-commerce; according to the US agency, virtual trade will showcase local products to international buyers, where catalogues and prices can be exchanged to enhance potential deals with the US market.

a934.speaker: Mark White, Acting country representative of USAID
a934.speech: Explained AGOA as a unilateral trade preference program that provides tariff-free access into the United States for over 6400 qualifying exports from eligible sub-Saharan African countries, including Namibia; said the USAID TradeHub is working with export-ready Namibian firms to meet US market entry requirements, engage prospective buyers and support the facilitation of trade deals ; “This strategy includes supporting exports and diversifying exports from Namibia to the United States for leather accessories, handicrafts and accessories, dates, meat and meat products, speciality foods, and cosmetics” ; assured that the US government will continue to support Namibian firms with market entry and trade-enhancing services to increase exports from these priority sectors ; “USAID is aiding export-ready firms in Namibia to participate in both physical and virtual market linkage and business-to-business events to engage with potential buyers to showcase their products and start business discussions. These linkages have already led to export deals. We are also building awareness about Namibian firms' export market achievements through these collaborations.”

a934.speaker: Key players such as the trade ministry and other stakeholders (AGOA strategy document)
a934.speech: In the AGOA strategy, highlighted priority sectors where Namibia has a competitive advantage or a potential advantage.

a934.speaker: Verna Sinimbo, Deputy Minister of Trade of Namibia
a934.speech: Said the strategy and action plan will help Namibia develop her competitiveness by taking advantage of the Generalised System of Preference (GSP) offered under the AGOA regime, which provides eligible countries with duty-free access to the US market: “Namibia, as a country, will look forward to the initiatives and ideas that will assist the country to derive new focus that will improve and expand Namibia's export basket to the USA market.”

a1074.speaker: U.S. Mission in Nigeria (statement)
a1074.speech: A statement made available to journalists on Wednesday by the U.S. Mission said that the hub offers training in various technical skills, including robotics, digital marketing, mobile app development, web development, photography, and videography; it added that it also provides important health information, focusing on HIV prevention and sexual health, and that for young people with HIV the hub offers support to help them follow their treatment plans.

a1074.speaker: David Greene, Deputy Chief of Mission for the U.S. Embassy in Nigeria
a1074.speech: "This tech hub is more than just a learning center; it is a safe space where young people can learn, grow, and develop skills that will serve them for life." He added that the project aims to create economic opportunities and nurture future leaders.

a1074.speaker: Cole Gbolahan, U.S. CDC Nigeria Deputy Director for Partner Management
a1074.speech: Explained that the hub helps young people develop personally and economically, giving them skills for the digital economy and beyond.

a1079.speaker: Dk Mwigulu Nchemba, Tanzanian Minister of Finance
a1079.speech: Speaking after signing the loan agreement between the Ministry of Finance and Jica, said implementation of the project will spur growth of the agriculture sector by increasing production for farmers through access to affordable capital. He said medium- and long-term loans will be given to farmers, production groups and agriculture-related institutions to enable them to invest in modern farming, obtain better inputs and advanced agricultural technology. "Access to agricultural capital will also enable farmers to have mixed crops and climate-resilient agriculture, which will contribute to food security, rural development and the strength of the economy as a whole," he said. He said implementation of this project is in line with the Five-Year Development Plan and with the Second Agricultural Sector Development Programme.

a1079.speaker: Dk Mwigulu Nchemba, Tanzanian Minister of Finance
a1079.speech: "So, you can see how important this funding is. I would like to assure you that the Government of the United Republic of Tanzania will take all necessary steps to ensure this project is implemented effectively so as to achieve the intended goals," he said. He said Tanzania recognises and is grateful for the funding that has been provided by the Government of Japan and implemented by Jica. "This long-standing relationship has contributed greatly to stimulating sustainable economic growth and improving the lives of Tanzanians. The Japanese Government's readiness to spur economic growth and to continue strengthening cooperation is exemplary. The Government of Tanzania will continue this cooperation in order to achieve our shared goals," he said.

a1079.speaker: Frank Nyabundege, Managing Director of TADB
a1079.speech: Said the availability of these funds is a continuation of what is being done in agriculture. He said that since the sixth-phase government came to power more than Sh954 billion has been channelled to TADB to ensure that many Tanzanians benefit from agriculture by moving them from subsistence to commercial farming. "The Government has been supporting the agriculture sector so that it can perform well and our colleagues say if you want to get rich go into agriculture," he said. He said the funds will be issued at low interest to enable smallholder farmers to afford them so they can farm productively and lift themselves economically. "Investing a lot of money aims to ensure that the agriculture sector in the country is productive for Tanzanians because 65 percent are there, so we see how important it is to carry the agriculture sector so that Tanzanians' lives improve," he said.

a1079.speaker: Katsura Miyazaki, Vice President of Jica
a1079.speech: Said the project aims to contribute to improving agricultural productivity, increasing farmers' incomes and adding value in the value chain of the four priority crops. "The four priority crops are rice, maize, wheat and sunflower, which are listed in the Tanzanian Government's Five-Year Development Plan (FYDP III), and it will strengthen the value chain and food security," he said. He said the funds will also finance the horticulture sector and create employment opportunities for women and youth.

a1268.speaker: Her Excellency Ana Nembe, head of the African Union (AU) delegation to Liberia
a1268.speech: Expressed the AU's unwavering commitment to supporting Liberia in its time of need and emphasized that the donation underscores the AU's dedication to regional solidarity and humanitarian support. "This gesture is a testament to the African Union's principle of collective support and our deep concern for our brothers and sisters in Liberia who are facing immense challenges due to the recent floods. The AU stands with Liberia, and we hope this contribution will bring some relief to the affected communities," said Madam Nembe.

a1268.speaker: Honorable Gabriel H. Salee, Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a1268.speech: Conveyed heartfelt gratitude to the African Union for its timely assistance: "On behalf of His Excellency President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and the people of Liberia, I extend our deepest appreciation to the African Union for this generous donation. The funds will be utilized for the intended purpose, ensuring that the flood victims receive the necessary assistance to rebuild their lives." ; He further noted that the African Union's support demonstrates the importance of collective efforts in addressing humanitarian crises across the continent.

a1268.speaker: Honorable Gabriel H. Salee, Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a1268.speech: Assured the AU delegation and the Liberian public that the government is committed to transparency and accountability in the disbursement and utilization of the funds. "The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will work closely with relevant stakeholders to ensure that every dollar of this contribution directly benefits the affected communities. We owe this to our citizens and to the African Union, whose trust we deeply value," he stated.

a1268.speaker: Honorable Gabriel H. Salee, Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs of Liberia
a1268.speech: Called on other regional and international partners to emulate the African Union's example by extending their support to Liberia: "While this contribution from the AU is a remarkable step forward, the scale of the disaster requires continued assistance from all quarters. Together, we can help our people recover and rebuild stronger communities," he urged.

a1317.speaker: Motherk Masire, mindfulness coach and session facilitator
a1317.speech: "Vision boarding isn't just about goals; it's about aligning your inner desires with the energy of creation."

a1317.speaker: Organisers of TatsoConnekt's Vision Board & Bubbly Brunch
a1317.speech: Described the event as a curated blend of mindfulness, manifestation, and networking, or as they put it, "Connekting, Connekting, Connekting."

a1370.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Mozambique, the U.S. Department of Defense and PEPFAR (joint statement)
a1370.speech: "hope this donation will not only benefit Mozambican military personnel but also their families, communities, and the people of Mozambique. The United States Government will continue working alongside the Government of the Republic of Mozambique as we fight to protect the people of Mozambique from the threats of COVID-19 and HIV/AIDS." Announced that the Embassy and the Department of Defense through USAFRICOM presented a donation of Personal Protective Equipment to Mozambique's Military Health, and that DHAPP and PEPFAR donated four mobile clinics to aid in the expansion of the Mozambican Armed Forces' male circumcision programme, a donation valued at US$172,461.

a1493.speaker: Observatory of Economic Complexity (data)
a1493.speech: According to data from the Observatory of Economic Complexity, Russian exports to The Gambia reached $11.5 million in 2022, consisting almost entirely of refined petroleum products, a significant increase from $2.36 million in 2017, growing at an annualized rate of 37.3% over the five years.

a1493.speaker: Sergey Lavrov, Russian Foreign Minister, and Mamadou Tangara, Gambian Foreign Minister
a1493.speech: During the January 2024 meeting between Foreign Ministers Lavrov and Tangara, both officials emphasized the importance of elevating economic ties to match the quality of political dialogue. Lavrov specifically noted, “It would be important to bring trade and economic ties to the level of our good political dialogue”, identifying areas such as construction, infrastructure modernization, transport, agriculture, and tourism as particularly promising sectors for collaboration.

a1493.speaker: Russian government
a1493.speech: Recently, Russia has pledged to increase scholarships for African students, particularly in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Russia also expressed interest in infrastructure modernization.

a1500.speaker: African Development Bank Group (AfDB report)
a1500.speech: said an AfDB report reported that United States Secretary of State Antony Blinken has praised the African Development Bank Group for the exceptional efforts it is undertaking to help Africa feed itself and the rest of the world.

a1500.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a1500.speech: "Extraordinary work is being done to get to a place where Africa feeds itself and a place where Africa feeds the world. I'm convinced that can happen." ; "The African Development Bank is making the necessary investments in sustainable production in a smart effective way and along with its AfricaRice programme maximising crops and producing crops that can stand up to climate change." ; "I applaud the Bank and your leadership for the powerful and inspiring impact of your initiatives. You are setting an example for others about how a bank is run."

a1500.speaker: Dr. Akinwunmi A. Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a1500.speech: "This is the first time that a US Secretary of State would visit the African Development Bank and its work. Secretary Blinken's visit is historic and provides great momentum for our work to feed Africa. I applaud Secretary Blinken's strong leadership and commitment to food security and look forward to working closely with him and the US government to advance our joint efforts to support Africa to feed itself and help feed the world." ; Thanking the US for its support to the Bank Group's key agricultural initiatives: "I applaud the work President Biden is doing for global food security. I'm delighted with the partnership we have with the US Government to help us move forward on food security in Africa." ; He also thanked Secretary Blinken for a new grant of $9.5 million to support the Bank's Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation initiative (TAAT).

a1509.speaker: Committee of Concerned Scientists (CCS)
a1509.speech: wrote two letters to the State Department a year ago asking then US Secretary of State Anthony Blinken to intervene in my situation and help stop the ongoing death threats and harassment that I have faced for some years now from operatives within the Sierra Leone government and their allied opposition groups. ; In July 2024, the CCS wrote a letter to the State Department requesting then US Secretary of State Anthony Blinken to intervene and "use the friendly relationship, including financial support, between Sierra Leone and the United States to obtain guarantee that [my] life would not be in danger if I returned to Sierra Leone." ; CCS sent a follow-up letter to Secretary Blinken requesting that the US government's financial commitment to Sierra Leone must include urging the country's leaders to respect human rights, including guaranteeing my safety and right to travel to Sierra Leone to pursue research.

a1509.speaker: Africanist Press investigative reports
a1509.speech: One of the reports showed that President Bio and his spouse spent allegedly more than US$750,000 of public funds on personal shopping. Another report also detailed how President Bio and First Lady Fatima Bio cumulatively withdrew over Le71.4 billion (about US$8 million) as international travel per diem in FY2022, violating the country's legal procedures. The reports also included revelations relating to misappropriation of public election funds by the country's electoral commission, and how opposition parties and parliament compromised the June 2023 Sierra Leone elections. ; An Africanist Press investigation discovered that the pseudo-strike by a supposed splinter group of teachers, the August 2022 protest, and subsequent incidents of violence in November 2023 were all orchestrated by state actors and allied opposition groups. ; We discovered and published evidence showing that Sierra Leonean officials paid at least US$5 million to cyber intelligence and private security firms to carry out censorship campaigns against me and Africanist Press.

a1509.speaker: A Catholic priest/clergyman in Sierra Leone (WhatsApp message)
a1509.speech: He threatened I would soon be killed and buried. He described how my bones would then be exhumed and ground into powder. This powder, he claimed, would be turned into Kush—a synthetic drug in West Africa allegedly made from human remains.

a1509.speaker: Bank of Sierra Leone (formal complaint, 20 April 2021)
a1509.speech: wrote a complaint against me and Africanist Press to the Attorney General and Minister of Justice in Sierra Leone, in which it alleged that Africanist Press illegally accessed and published information relating to banking transactions and details of President Julius Maada Bio's travel expenditures and budgetary allocations to the Office of the First Lady. The Complaint stated that the publications amounted to theft of property from the Bank of Sierra Leone and asked that "necessary" criminal action be taken against me for the publications. The Bank also alleged that these actions had the potential to compromise the nation's relationship with international partners.

a1509.speaker: Office of National Security (ONS) of Sierra Leone (complaint to the Independent Media Commission, 4 May 2022)
a1509.speech: stated that "most of the Africanist Press publications have been inherently inflammatory, either causing disaffection amongst the public or inciting them against the government." The ONS noted, in particular, that the Africanist Press had published information about the salaries and allowances of public sector workers which showed that the military was paid less than their peers in other sectors of the Sierra Leone civil service. The agency asked the Commission to dissuade Africanist Press from continued publication of so-called "inflammatory" articles.

a1509.speaker: General Kalokoh Media Team (Facebook group post, 23 May 2022)
a1509.speech: posted that the Africanist Press should face prosecution for cybercrimes. In its Facebook profile, the group stated that its purpose is to "promote the interest of the president," an apparent reference to President Julius Maada Bio.

a1509.speaker: Member of the ruling Sierra Leone People's Party (SLPP) and chairman of the board of directors of the Sierra Leone Cable Network (op-ed)
a1509.speech: published an op-ed stating that the government should treat Africanist Press as having committed treason.

a1509.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) and Civil Forum for Assets Recovery (CiFAR)
a1509.speech: issued statements in May 2022 calling on the Sierra Leone government to investigate the death threats and potential charges against me. These requests were ignored by government agencies the CPJ and CiFAR contacted and there has been no change in the impunity to date.

a1509.speaker: United States Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (announcement)
a1509.speech: announced in September 2024 that the US government had signed a US$480 million compact agreement with Sierra Leone's government to support the country's debt-strapped economy.

a1509.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a1509.speech: Following MCC's announcement, Secretary Blinken said the US government was committed to supporting democracy and accountability in Sierra Leone.

a1509.speaker: US State Department (non-response)
a1509.speech: It is possible that Secretary Blinken and State Department officials ignored the Committee's request. I am not aware that State Department officials responded to any of the Committee's letters.

a1509.speaker: About 200 academics from universities in Europe, United States, Africa and Asia (open letter, July 2024), endorsed by the Network of Concerned Historians (NCH), the Royal Netherlands Historical Society and Historians Without Borders (HWB)
a1509.speech: signed an open letter of support denouncing death threats and harassment orchestrated against me by Sierra Leonean leaders.

a1509.speaker: American Historical Association (AHA) (letter, September 2024)
a1509.speech: sent a letter to Sierra Leone's President Julius Maada Bio urging the "government to cease threatening [Bah] and to protect [Bah] from harassment and violence as it would any other citizen."

a1509.speaker: Sierra Leonean authorities (non-response)
a1509.speech: We learned that Sierra Leonean authorities also failed to respond to the AHA's letter. The government had likewise ignored all previous statements and requests from other international organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), Reporters Without Borders (RSF), and Endangered Scholars Worldwide (ESW).

a1509.speaker: US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) (announcement)
a1509.speech: In early May 2024 announced a US$412 million loan to the US-backed company, Milele Energy, and its corporate partner, TCQ Power Limited, to "boost Sierra Leone's energy sector." DFC also provided a US$150 million loan in support of a non-advertised infrastructure contract awarded to the Turkish-based Summa Group (now owned by FB Group) to expand and privately operate Sierra Leone's only international airport on a 25-year concession.

a1509.speaker: Jared Yancey, Deputy mission chief of the US Embassy in Freetown
a1509.speech: described the US security partnership with Sierra Leone as "groundbreaking," saying it is "specifically tailored to the unique environment and doctrine of the Republic of Sierra Leone Armed Forces."

a1509.speaker: A Sierra Leonean civil servant (anonymous)
a1509.speech: "the economic and security support that the Bio regime continues to receive from the United States has emboldened political figures to believe that they can suppress citizens and violate human rights with impunity."

a1509.speaker: Amnesty International (report, March 2023)
a1509.speech: reported that Sierra Leone's security forces allegedly killed and wounded protesters and bystanders when cracking down on demonstrations that erupted in Freetown, Makeni and Kamakwie in August 2022. Amnesty International specifically lamented the absence of justice for those injured or the families of those killed during the protests.

a1509.speaker: Cybersecurity and Crimes Act of Sierra Leone (law signed November 2021)
a1509.speech: ostensibly intended to prevent the "abusive use of computer systems [and] to provide a timely and effective collection of electronic evidence for the purpose of investigation and prosecution of cybercrime..."

a1509.speaker: Chernoh Alpha M. Bah, Sierra Leonean historian, investigative journalist and editor-in-chief of Africanist Press
a1509.speech: In August 2023, sent a letter to the State Department underlining the US obligation to ensure its continuous economic and security engagement with Sierra Leone include the protection of human rights, especially the right to free speech and academic freedom. ; Respectfully requested that democratic and human rights organizations re-engage the new State Department leadership and other elected representatives of the US government to ensure they directly request the Sierra Leonean government and political leaders to: (1) confirm my right to return to Sierra Leone and continue my work without fear of reprisals or criminal prosecution related to my work including my freedom of speech; and (2) remind the government of its obligation to investigate and address threats made against me. ; "We believe that the United States, as a leading partner of the government of Sierra Leone, has an obligation to ensure that its continuous engagement with the government of Sierra Leone involves safeguarding the fundamental rights of Sierra Leonean citizens, including the right to free speech, academic freedom, and freedom of the press."

a1595.speaker: Dr. Ernest Kombo, President of the Africa Hope Development Foundation
a1595.speech: said widows, widowers, and other vulnerable citizens need support and love, speaking at Kabbe North District where the Foundation handed over humanitarian assistance to widows, people with disabilities, and the elderly ; pledged his organisation to assist the needy households and refugees flocking to Namibia through the Katima Mulilo Border Post, as well as widows ; "Therefore, it is imperative and incumbent upon us that we exert ourselves in helping our beneficiaries to be strengthened in their areas of need, so as to enable them to be responsible enough to sustain themselves while maintaining their dignity and self-worth."

a1595.speaker: Moffat Sileze, Swapo Party Coordinator for the Zambezi Region
a1595.speech: lauded the Foundation for helping the needy.

a1636.speaker: Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Mali
a1636.speech: Confirmed that the Prime Ministers decided to meet first to exchange information about their countries, but also to share their analyses regarding this 80th UN General Assembly, the state of the world and the aspirations of the peoples of the Confederation of Sahel States, which is to be able to take charge of themselves, for greater independence and sovereignty of their States and a break with practices that clash with the interests of their populations. To this end, he clarified, the Prime Ministers reviewed the activities they will undertake collectively so that the Confederation of Sahel States can carry the voice and the aspirations of the peoples of Burkina, Mali and Niger to the rostrum of the UN General Assembly in solidarity. "They consulted on a certain number of actions they will undertake here in New York, which also involve meeting the AES communities residing in the United States of America. They also welcomed all the progress recorded by the Confederation under the leadership of our Heads of State, namely Their Excellencies Army General Assimi Goita, Captain Ibrahim Traore, and Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, who had this brilliant idea of establishing this form of collaboration between our countries so that we can continue to work together." ; The Malian diplomat also indicated that the AES heads of government renewed their commitment to continue working in solidarity, to coordinate their teams and keep them mobilised until the final objective is achieved, that of dignity, sovereignty, but also the prosperity of their peoples.

a1695.speaker: Qatar, in a statement delivered by Turki Mohammed Abdullah al-Khalifa, Third Secretary in the African Affairs Department at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a1695.speech: Called on the international community to continue and increase the provision of humanitarian and developmental aid and technical assistance to strengthen the human rights capacity-building efforts of the Federal Republic of Somalia and implement its national and international obligations in alignment with its priorities.

a1695.speaker: Turki Mohammed Abdullah al-Khalifa, Third Secretary in the African Affairs Department, Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a1695.speech: Praised the launch of the national reconciliation framework, Somalia's accession to the UN Convention against Corruption, and the measures taken to promote the rights of women, children, and persons with disabilities.

a1695.speaker: Turki Mohammed Abdullah al-Khalifa, Third Secretary in the African Affairs Department, Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a1695.speech: Noted Qatar's keenness to provide various forms of aid and humanitarian assistance to Somalia, highlighting the signing of several agreements aimed at developing the education and health sectors, supporting strategic development projects, enhancing disaster management capacities, and fostering security and stability, in addition to rehabilitating government institutions and facilities.

a1836.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Eswatini Minister for Agriculture
a1836.speech: Shared the developments during a press briefing, confirming that government, through the National Maize Corporation (NMC), has activated its nationwide support network ahead of the ploughing season: "Government is fully prepared to assist farmers through the NMC, extension officers and other avenues. The farming season has begun, and all systems are in place to ensure that no farmer is left behind." ; announced that the network of agro-dealers has been expanded across all four regions to make it easier for farmers to access inputs closer to their homesteads; stressed that the subsidy programme remains targeted at genuinely deserving farmers who meet the eligibility criteria set out earlier in the year.

a1836.speaker: Mavela Vilane, National Maize Corporation (NMC) CEO
a1836.speech: "The land leased from emaSwati will be used to intensify government's maize production efforts. This is a key part of our plan to achieve food sovereignty and build resilience in our national grain reserves" ; noted that the maize produced from these leased fields would supplement supplies to the national strategic grain reserve, enhancing food security and stabilising prices in times of shortage.

a1836.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Eswatini Minister for Agriculture
a1836.speech: Confirmed a new foot and mouth disease (FMD) outbreak at Mambane during a press briefing at the ministry: "While we were celebrating our success in bringing the situation under control in the Shiselweni Region, an incursion was reported at Mambane. The outbreak was sparked by livestock that entered Eswatini from South Africa." ; stressed that authorities are working tirelessly to prevent the disease from spreading further into the Shiselweni Region and beyond, particularly through intensified vaccination and animal movement control: "We are now fighting the Mambane incursion head-on. The situation is under close monitoring and containment measures have been tightened."

a1849.speaker: Taylor Randall, President of the University of Utah
a1849.speech: "As Presidential Societal Impact Scholars, these exceptional faculty demonstrate how public engagement and scholarship can have a broad impact on the world around us. ; As one of the nation's leading research universities, we aim to improve the communities we serve by sharing our research and expertise in meaningful ways. The recipients of this award embody this mission, translating their work into efforts that not only shape their fields but also positively transform society."

a1919.speaker: World Economic Forum (WEF)
a1919.speech: recognises Namibia as one of the countries in Africa with the highest quality roads, with the country maintaining its leading position in road infrastructure on the continent for the fifth consecutive year.

a1919.speaker: Ambassador Albertus !Aochamub
a1919.speech: says that there is a global disparity in the recognition of UNESCO World Heritage sites, emphasising the significant imbalance between African and European countries.

a1919.speaker: Marie France Uwase, Communication Officer of the World Health Organisation's Africa Regional Office
a1919.speech: revealed at a media briefing on the preparations for the upcoming First Africa Health Workforce Investment Forum that Africa has a shortage of 5.3 million health workers, that achieving universal health coverage by 2030 will require an additional 1.8 million health workers, and that the continent is projected to have a critical shortage of about 6.1 million health workers by 2030.

a1919.speaker: World Press Freedom Index, Reporters Without Borders
a1919.speech: According to the latest annual World Press Freedom Index, Namibia's press freedom rankings dropped to second place in Africa and to 34th position from 22 globally, with Mauritania now ranking first in Africa.

a1919.speaker: Professor Yemi Osibanjo, former Nigerian Vice President
a1919.speech: states that Africa's low carbon footprint can be an advantage in developing green fuel and clean energy.

a1996.speaker: UNICEF report (released Wednesday evening)
a1996.speech: found that more than one in four children lives in “severe food poverty” — more than 180 million children are at risk of suffering serious health consequences without a nutritious and diversified diet; 440 million children under 5 (66%) in around a hundred low- and middle-income countries analysed do not have access to five food groups every day, and about 181 million (27%) consume at most foods from two groups; severe food poverty is concentrated in 20 countries, with particularly worrying situations in Somalia (63%), the Republic of Guinea (54%), Guinea-Bissau (53%) and Afghanistan (49%); the report pays special attention to the Gaza Strip, where the Israeli offensive triggered by Hamas’s 7 October attack led to the “collapse of the food and health systems”; noting only “slow progress” over the last 10 years, it advocated social protection mechanisms and humanitarian aid for the most vulnerable, and a transformation of the agri-food system, holding responsible high-sugar drinks and ultra-processed industrial dishes “aggressively marketed to families and which have become the norm for feeding children.”

a1996.speaker: UNICEF (dietary recommendations)
a1996.speech: recommends that young children consume daily foods from at least five of the eight food groups (breast milk, cereals, fruits and vegetables rich in vitamin A, meat or fish, eggs, dairy products, legumes, other fruits and vegetables).

a1996.speaker: Harriet Torlesse, one of the authors of the UNICEF report (to France-Presse)
a1996.speech: said a “shocking number” of children “survive on a very poor diet, consuming products from two or fewer food groups” ; explained that these children survive and grow, but “do not thrive. They are less successful at school and, as adults, they have more difficulty earning a living, which maintains a cycle of poverty from generation to generation” ; insisted that “the brain, the heart and the immune system, which are important for development and protection against disease, depend on vitamins, minerals and proteins” ; stressed that ultra-processed products are often “cheap, but also very caloric, very salty and fatty. They suppress hunger, but do not provide the vitamins and minerals that children need.”

a1996.speaker: Catherine Russell, Director of UNICEF (statement)
a1996.speech: warned that “children who eat only two food groups a day, for example rice and a little milk, are 50% more likely to suffer from severe forms of malnutrition,” such as wasting and extreme emaciation, which can lead to death.

a2084.speaker: Jean Sendeza, Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare of Malawi
a2084.speech: Urged women cross-border traders to familiarise themselves with existing trade laws, regulations and agreements to protect their interests: "Women cross-border traders try to cut corners because they are not familiar with the opportunities provided by trade agreements. They try to cut corners and end up losing more in bribes or penalties. We [local authorities] have to promote awareness to protect these women."

a2084.speaker: 2019 Malawi FinScope MSME Survey (report)
a2084.speech: Estimates that the MSME sector contributes about 40 percent to gross domestic product (GDP) and 24 percent of employment and that about 21 percent of the country's adult population derives their livelihood from the sector.

a2084.speaker: World Bank (analysis)
a2084.speech: An analysis by the World Bank shows that MSMEs, including cross-border traders have potential to contribute more to the economy, but their capacity to expand remains low because they do not have the same access to knowledge and networks as larger businesses.

a2084.speaker: Martha Kamchacha, conference chairperson, Women in Cross-Border Trade Conference
a2084.speech: Bemoaned bureaucracies and bottlenecks that traders face when transporting goods across borders: "We do not have the infrastructure and simplified procedures to help us expedite border processes. We end up taking too long at the border, which is a problem for our business, considering that crossing the border is a key component of our business."

a2084.speaker: Steven Yohane, Cross-Border Traders Association president
a2084.speech: Said they have already moved to address the knowledge gaps among local small-scale traders, saying the conference is one of the measures to orient traders on existing opportunities: "One of our biggest challenges is access to finance. We intend to use this meeting to provide information on initiatives and opportunities offered by the World Bank, through Agcom and the National Economic Empowerment Fund."

a2246.speaker: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI) of Liberia (statement)
a2246.speech: Expressed utmost concern over recent reports suggesting the presence of damaged rice involving some importers, and said it recognizes the urgency of this matter and has launched a full investigation through our Inspectorate Division to examine these claims, particularly as they relate to certain importers and suppliers ; stated that its inspection teams are conducting rigorous checks to identify and remove any compromised products, and we assure the public that all findings will be promptly and transparently shared ; "Anyone found to be responsible for distributing expired or contaminated goods will face the appropriate punitive measures in keeping law."

a2246.speaker: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI) of Liberia (statement)
a2246.speech: Said it is committed to enforcing the highest consumer protection and safety standards: "Protecting the health and welfare of the Liberian people is our foremost priority, and we are taking strong measures to enhance the capacity and effectiveness of our inspection and oversight regime. We are dedicated to holding importers, wholesalers, and retailers accountable, ensuring that only safe, high-quality products reach our citizens."

a2246.speaker: Commerce authorities of Liberia (statement)
a2246.speech: Called on citizens to join in this effort by reporting expired or suspicious products found in the market to our offices or through designated hotlines: "Together, we can maintain a safer, healthier market for all Liberians. The Ministry is unwavering in its commitment to consumer safety and will continue to work tirelessly to safeguard the quality of goods."

a2347.speaker: Center for Global Development (CGD)
a2347.speech: Based on the data presented to the US Congress on March 27, calculated how much American aid different countries of the world had lost; in addition to absolute values and shares of total USAID funding, experts estimated the losses for the GNI of each of the recipient countries.

a2347.speaker: The Africa Report
a2347.speech: Has systematized CGD data for African countries, listing losses country by country (Ethiopia: $386.9 million, or 30% of USAID funding and 0.24% of GNI; DR Congo: $386.7 million; Uganda: $306.8 million; South Africa: $260.6 million; Kenya: $224.7 million; and others), showing that nine countries have completely lost USAID assistance and that Liberia, whose funding has been cut by 98%, will lose a significant share of GNI (2.59%).

a2352.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a2352.speech: Declared on Tuesday that he was ready for direct negotiations with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin and other leaders in order to end the war launched by the Kremlin almost three years ago; replied that he would negotiate with Putin "if it is the only configuration in which we can bring peace to the citizens of Ukraine and no longer lose people" and that in that case "we will accept this configuration, this meeting with four participants."

a2352.speaker: Piers Morgan, British presenter
a2352.speech: Asked about the possibility of negotiating with Vladimir Putin and had earlier raised the hypothesis of negotiations between Ukraine, Russia, the United States and the European Union.

a2352.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2352.speech: Criticised American aid spending to Ukraine during his campaign.

a2352.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a2352.speech: Declared at the end of January that he was open to negotiations to end the conflict in Ukraine, while rejecting direct discussions with Volodymyr Zelensky and stating that he saw no "will" on Kyiv part: if the Ukrainian president "wants to take part in negotiations, I will choose the people who will conduct those negotiations," judging him "illegitimate."

a2352.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a2352.speech: Maintains that any potential peace agreement should contain solid security guarantees for his country from Western countries.

a2352.speaker: The Kremlin
a2352.speech: Is essentially demanding Ukraine surrender, that it give up joining NATO and that Russia keep the Ukrainian territories whose annexation it has claimed.

a2590.speaker: Professor Samuel Bumie Ovuru, Professor of Public Administration, Highstone Global University, Texas
a2590.speech: “I am truly elated to be elevated to the professorial cadre by the Highstone Global University, Texas USA. It brings a sense of fulfillment to have risen to the zenith of academic qualification rising from the shackles of poverty and deprivation of my humble beginning. The elevation also brings with it a weight of responsibility for shaping the present and future public administrators in Nigeria, to contribute my quota in making the public institutions in developing countries work properly and efficiently.”

a2590.speaker: Professor Samuel Bumie Ovuru, Professor of Public Administration, Highstone Global University, Texas
a2590.speech: Said on the cost of governance: “The issue of cost of governance normally involves two costs. The first is cost associated with running the government, while the second is the cost incurred by the government in the course of providing goods and services... the issue should be discussed from a wider perspective than the high-cost angle, which most people focus on without taking into consideration the peculiarities we have as a country in terms of our population, ethnic colouration, diverse linguistic groupings and the need for inclusiveness.” ; “The truth is that for Nigeria, the cost of governance has relatively been the same with marginal growth since independence while our population has been growing astronomically without corresponding growth in our income... There is therefore the need for the Nigerian government in all its tiers to reduce this cost element drastically with the introduction of electronic government in its structure and digital tools in its operations.”

a2590.speaker: Professor Samuel Bumie Ovuru, Professor of Public Administration, Highstone Global University, Texas
a2590.speech: Said on hunger and food security: “The number of Nigerians living below the poverty line is more than 26 million... Let us look at the root cause of hunger in the land. Which in my opinion is caused by insurgency, flooding, craving for white collar jobs, migration from rural areas to urban areas, climate change, unemployment, high food prices, etc.” ; “One of the major problems in Nigeria is disunity. This is what is giving impetus to insurgency. Sixty-four years after independence, we still see ourselves first as belonging to our tribal groupings and least as Nigerians.” ; “Another way to secure food security in Nigeria is to make agriculture more lucrative... We should also harness the work and innovations from the over 15 National Agricultural Research Institutes in Nigeria.”

a2590.speaker: Professor Samuel Bumie Ovuru, Professor of Public Administration, Highstone Global University, Texas
a2590.speech: Said on tuition fees and education: “An increase in tuition fees by a university would only marginally increase the revenue of that university. The wealthiest universities in the world like Harvard University, MIT, Yale University do not make their wealth only from tuition fees, rather they make their money from other sources such as endowment, sale of patents, sponsored research, grants, donations and provision of other services like hospitals. It is therefore necessary for Nigerian universities to explore all areas of the revenue spectrum in higher education to increase their revenues.” ; Listed the challenges facing the educational sector as “poor funding, diminishing number of qualified teachers due to brain drain, reduction in the standard of education, cultism in schools, high incidence of examination misconduct, failing infrastructure and facilities.”

a2590.speaker: Professor Samuel Bumie Ovuru, Professor of Public Administration, Highstone Global University, Texas
a2590.speech: Said on foreign investors leaving Nigeria: “We are really witnessing the relocation of foreign businesses from Nigeria even to neighbouring countries and this is not good for the country because of its negative impact on our economy... the reasons cited by foreigners and local business owners for leaving the country are the harsh business operating environment, hostile and frequent harassment from host communities, high incidence of insecurity, and the high level of political and policy instability in Nigeria.” ; “We must note that to implement these things takes some time. That is why we must be patient with the government and lend our support to ensure that things work in Nigeria.”

a2590.speaker: Professor Samuel Bumie Ovuru, Professor of Public Administration, Highstone Global University, Texas
a2590.speech: Said on the #EndBadGovernance youth protests: “To reduce protests by the youths the government should engage meaningfully with the youths. More employment opportunities need to be created to also engage them... This culture of get-rich-quick is limiting our youths from seeing opportunities that abound in Nigeria. The Federal Government’s initiative for youth empowerment which is Nigeria Youth Investment Fund (NYIF) should be given more publicity... Above all, the government should provide financial grants for start-ups for youths in Nigeria.”

a2590.speaker: National Bureau of Statistics Multidimensional Poverty Index survey of 2022
a2590.speech: Revealed that 63% of persons living within Nigeria (133 million people as at 2022) are multidimensionally poor.

a2590.speaker: United Nations report
a2590.speech: Reported that 26 million Nigerians are hungry.

a2866.speaker: Foster Mohale, spokesperson for South Africa's national health department
a2866.speech: Says the national health department, which receives Pepfar funding that makes up 17% of the department's HIV budget, has not received a waiver letter. “We are, however, aware of the communication on the waiver, which was received by their partners”

a2866.speaker: US Embassy and Consulates in South Africa
a2866.speech: Announced on Monday that Pepfar-funded projects could still apply for waivers

a2866.speaker: US President Donald Trump (executive order)
a2866.speech: Signed an executive order on 7 February that cancelled all funding from his government for South Africa for what he labels as “unjust and immoral practices” of South Africa that “harm our nation [the US]”

a2866.speaker: Trump administration (waiver rules/guidelines)
a2866.speech: Approved activities have to directly relate to “the delivery of lifesaving HIV care and treatment services”, which, according to the Trump administration, don't include HIV prevention services, unless they are for pregnant or breastfeeding women

a2866.speaker: South African health department spokesperson
a2866.speech: Said Pepfar was going to fund the roll-out of 520 123 anti-HIV pill “initiations” this year, with the government paying for the pills while Pepfar funded the salaries of health workers employed by NGOs who administered the tablets, as well as the cost of data collectors and outreach campaigns

a2866.speaker: Pepfar waiver letters (USAID and CDC)
a2866.speech: Instructed projects funded through the CDC to submit work plans and adjusted budgets up to 19 April and those funded through USAID to submit a plan and budget for 30 days; the letters make clear that no project can restart work until their USAID or CDC project officer has reviewed and approved their new work plans and budgets in writing; organisations have to provide monthly written confirmation, on an official letterhead, that they will only continue with activities that qualify for the waiver and not roll out any “related to abortion services, family planning, conferences, administrative costs outside the scope of the limited waiver, gender ideology or diversity, equity and inclusion programmes (DEI), transgender surgeries or other forms of non-lifesaving assistance”; the letters also specify that funds that would have been used for now-disallowed activities can't be used for approved activities, while incurred costs before 24 January and costs associated with the stop-work order, labour-law compliance and “the security of assets” can be claimed

a2866.speaker: One of the founders of an affected organisation (anonymous, fears losing funds)
a2866.speech: “But the reality check is that I don't think any of the organisations can actually restart, whatever the instruction is, until they receive the funds in the bank. Everyone has exhausted their reserves.”

a2866.speaker: One project leader (anonymous)
a2866.speech: “The confusion arrives because DEI is not defined in any executive order, and there are vague terms like 'gender ideology' We have no real confirmation of that until someone actually gives approval.”

a2866.speaker: Pepfar waiver Frequently Asked Questions document, issued 10 February
a2866.speech: Explains that Pepfar will only fund HIV testing for pregnant and breastfeeding women and their babies, and to find out if someone needs treatment, and that no HIV testing before medical circumcision or to establish HIV-negative status before preventive medication is allowed; says social and behavioural change communication activities are not covered by the waiver; and says Pepfar officials may, at this stage, only discuss “high level talking points” to be provided by the department of state, with civil society organisations, and that “talking points and press guidance are under development”

a2866.speaker: Avac (New York-based HIV advocacy organisation) and the Journalism Development Network (lawsuit)
a2866.speech: Filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration on Monday, arguing that it froze foreign funding “illegally and unconscionably”

a2866.speaker: Mitchell Warren, executive director of Avac
a2866.speech: “We don't expect to see our funding renewed any time soon, if ever. But we filed the case to make the point that the actions of this new administration defy logic, defy science and actually defy the US legal system. We know that foreign assistance is going to change. We know that Pepfar is going to change. We know that all programmes should be reviewed and re-evaluated, but they need to be done with clarity, with a strategy and clear metrics.” ; “What we're trying to do is to get the freeze on foreign assistance stopped, and then let's all talk together, implementers, governments, the United States administration, of what the future can look like, not only for Pepfar and the Aids response, but for global health and development. There is much riding on this; it can't be dictated by executive orders.”

a2877.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a2877.speech: "I am really glad to have been joined today by the UN family, an important body in overseeing global issues from politics, peace and stability and, equally important, development, because what we are looking at at all times is how to bring about sustainable development in taking care of the well-being of the citizens of the world, so I am really glad we found time to meet."

a2877.speaker: United Nations in Namibia
a2877.speech: Says that the strategies to reduce unemployment, particularly among youth, poverty, and income inequalities, resonate closely with its overarching objectives.

a2877.speaker: Hopolang Phororo, UN Resident Coordinator in Namibia
a2877.speech: Revealed that the UN has managed to mobilise financial resources through the Sustainable Development Goal Fund ; "And we are implementing that through the Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions, and this is part of what President Hage Geingob had requested: Namibia to be a pathfinder country. So we are then continuing to work with various government ministries on addressing this employment situation, looking at the biomass sector and seeking how we can be able to have that catalytic impact." ; "That is to complement this first tranche of resources that we are talking about. The first one was to the tune of 1.8 million, and the second one, we are talking about a tranche of about a million US dollars, and for the second tranche, we will work also closely with the World Bank, so that is the first point - just to say that we are really eager to collaborate with the government in bringing the technical expertise."

a2890.speaker: Government of Malawi (statement signed by Chief Secretary Justin Saidi)
a2890.speech: Reads the statement in part: “The President of the Republic of Malawi, has noted with grave concern the impact of food insecurity as a result of cumulative impacts of prolonged dry spells, high commodity prices and other macroeconomic as highlighted by the recently released Food Situation Report by the Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee. “In view of this, His Excellency has exercised the powers vested in him under Section 37 (1) of the Disaster Risk Management Act (2023) and declared a State of disaster in the affected areas.” ; Government has appealed to local and international support for the affected families.

a2890.speaker: Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee (Mvac) report
a2890.speech: Indicated that about four million people are at risk of hunger during the 2025/26 consumption period, representing 22 percent of the country’s projected population of 18.5 million; according to the Mvac report, the vulnerable population would require humanitarian food assistance amounting to roughly 200 000 metric tonnes (MT) of maize, estimated at K387.20 billion, for a period ranging between three and six months.

a2890.speaker: Government of Malawi
a2890.speech: Has indicated that it is facilitating the provision of humanitarian assistance to the affected districts, while intensifying irrigation farming and other interventions to address the situation.

a2890.speaker: Wilson Moleni, Commissioner for the Department of Disaster Management Affairs (Dodma)
a2890.speech: Said the department has developed the 2025/26 Lean Season Food Insecurity Response Plan; said government will on Saturday, November 1, launch the distribution of free maize and cash to over four million people facing food shortages in response to a recent Mvac report which indicated that the situation is expected to worsen until the next harvest season in March 2026 ; Said Moleni: “The declaration gives us an opportunity to start working in areas that are in dire need and the nation in general. The response will not only target the declared districts but all districts depending on the severity of hunger as indicated in the Mvac report. “The affected people will receive food assistance and cash through the Social Cash Transfer Programme to be implemented by the government and our partners.” ; He said the 11 districts declared as disaster areas have about 20 percent of their populations food insecure, adding that the declaration will open doors for more partners to help.

a2890.speaker: Agnes Nyirongo, Centre for Social Concern project officer
a2890.speech: Called on the government to prepare adequately to avoid declaring yet another State of Disaster next year; she tipped government to consider supplying drought resistant and early maturing seed varieties as it provides farm inputs ; Said Nyirongo: “This is essential because in recent years, Malawi has struggled with the effects of climate change. Preparing well in advance is a step in the right direction.”

a2911.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect (post on his Truth Social media platform)
a2911.speech: Announced that Nikki Haley, former US ambassador to the UN, will not join his new administration, and also said Mike Pompeo would not return to his Cabinet: “I will not be inviting former Ambassador Nikki Haley or former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo to join the Trump Administration, which is currently in formation,” before adding his appreciation for their service to the country.

a2922.speaker: Elvis Ncube, National Bakers Association of Zimbabwe president
a2922.speech: Said recent commissioning of plants and ongoing investment in local production signal a positive outlook for the sector: “What we are witnessing in the baking sector is very encouraging. Local bakers and producers are commissioning new plants, and we anticipate more facilities coming online in the near future. This clearly shows that the industry is on a growth trajectory.” ; “These are Zimbabweans, living and investing here, and they deserve support and appropriate incentives to continue driving industrial growth. Too often, discussions about investors focus on international players, yet we have local entrepreneurs who are building this country’s future.”

a2922.speaker: Elvis Ncube, National Bakers Association of Zimbabwe president
a2922.speech: Said one of the key priorities for the industry remains ensuring bread remains affordable for the average Zimbabwean, and urged the government to consider reinstating zero-rated tax status on bread to achieve more growth: “It is our plea that bread be made tax-exempt again. This will help us stabilize prices and ensure the product stays within reach of all Zimbabweans, provided other input costs remain stable. The outlook is generally good. What we need now is to protect and sustain the gains being made so that every Zimbabwean continues to benefit.”

a3084.speaker: National Development Plan (NDP6)
a3084.speech: According to the latest figures contained in NDP6, out of about 455,000 youth in the country’s labour force, about 253,000 are in full-time or gainful employment, while the remaining 202,000, about 44.4%, are still without jobs; Namibia’s entire labour force stood at 867,247 in 2023, of which 546,805 were gainfully employed and 320,442 unemployed, down from 364,411 unemployed in 2018.

a3084.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a3084.speech: Plans, under NDP6, to increase the employment rate to 75% through various policy interventions, and says Namibia is expected to achieve an annual economic growth rate of 7% or more by the end of the 2030/31 financial period.

a3084.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a3084.speech: “This sub-goal aims to achieve high and inclusive economic growth with employment growing faster than the growth of entrants into the labour market, thus reducing the unemployment rate. This strategy focuses on the mechanisation and modernisation of agriculture, especially subsistence farming, to erase dichotomy and increase production to meet local demand and exports. This requires coordination and collaboration between the public sector, private sector and research and higher education institutions,” the President said when she recently launched NDP6.

a3084.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a3084.speech: Plans to support and embrace new industries by fast-tracking legislation in emerging sectors such as oil and gas, green industries, the blue economy, nuclear energy and others, to create certainty and an enabling environment for promoters and investors ; “It further aims to enhance public sector coordination to remove barriers and ensure seamless execution of projects without compromising the environment and the well-being of the Namibian people. This strategy seeks to promote both domestic and foreign investment in productive economic sectors by creating a conducive environment through facilitation, coordination and legislation.” ; “These will include actions such as improving the ease of doing business, enhancing skills availability and industry absorption, strengthening innovation capabilities, reinforcing the institutional framework, and improving business legislation.”

a3271.speaker: Joseph Ng'ang'a, Interim CEO of the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP)
a3271.speech: Said the role of reliable power in enabling irrigation and clean drinking water is critical, improving livelihoods and local economies.

a3352.speaker: Latest financial disclosures from Malawi's top publicly listed companies
a3352.speech: Show an optimistic picture for the country's economy, with several key players reporting record profits; NICO Holdings PLC has emerged as the most profitable company in Malawi, with an estimated profit after tax of between MK122 billion and MK131 billion for 2024, growth of 110% to 126% compared to 2023; FDH Bank, NBS Bank, and National Bank of Malawi recorded profit increases of 66% to 146%.

a3352.speaker: FDH Bank (profit forecast)
a3352.speech: Expects a profit surge of between MK36.3 billion and MK38.3 billion, representing growth of 127% to 146% compared to last year.

a3352.speaker: Airtel Malawi PLC (profit forecast)
a3352.speech: Forecasting a profit increase exceeding 400% from 2023.

a3405.speaker: International Trade Centre
a3405.speech: Has said aid for trade cannot work as the direction of future official development assistance (ODA) decisions by governments remains hazy.

a3405.speaker: Pamela Coke-Hamilton, Executive Director of the International Trade Centre
a3405.speech: Said in her contribution to the 2025 Ibrahim Forum Report: Financing The Africa We Want that since the year began, over 150 restrictive trade measures have been put in place by governments, with more feared to be on the horizon; said concerns over the stability of the international trading system are now running rampant, with any disruptions coming at real costs for those who can least afford it ; "The field of international development has been turned upside down, even as some of the more recent shifts often reflect an intensification of longer-running trends. Many aid budgets have been cut, while many donors are shifting their priorities to meet a wide range of demands and continue living up to their commitments to their taxpayers."

a3405.speaker: Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD projections)
a3405.speech: According to the OECD's latest projections, ODA cuts that governments have announced in 2025 could amount to between a nine and 17 percent drop from last year's ODA levels.

a3405.speaker: Pamela Coke-Hamilton, Executive Director of the International Trade Centre
a3405.speech: "That is where agreements like the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) come in. The AfCFTA's potential economic gains are immense: if tariffs within the continent are fully slashed, intra-African trade could grow by an impressive $22 billion by 2029."

a3405.speaker: Patrick Botha, Ministry of Industry and Trade spokesperson (Malawi)
a3405.speech: Said the ministry and AfCFTA secretariat will be helping local firms with export guidance under the Guided Trade Initiative once they are ready.

a3405.speaker: Daisy Kambalame, Chief Executive Officer of the Malawi Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MCCCI)
a3405.speech: Said while lack of information is slowing the uptake of the AfCFTA pilot initiative, "challenges facing the businesses sector could make Malawian goods and services uncompetitive."

a3423.speaker: Canada (government announcement)
a3423.speech: Has announced it is lifting a freeze on funding for the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA), after facing fierce criticism for cutting assistance during Israel's war in Gaza.

a3423.speaker: Ahmed Hussen, Canadian Minister of International Development (statement)
a3423.speech: Said in a statement on Friday that the government is "resuming its funding to UNRWA so more can be done to respond to the urgent needs of Palestinian civilians".

a3423.speaker: Israel (government)
a3423.speech: Accused about a dozen of the agency's more than 13,000 employees in Gaza of taking part in a Hamas attack on October 7.

a3423.speaker: UNRWA (UN agency for Palestinian refugees)
a3423.speech: Immediately sacked the employees in question and announced that it was opening a probe into the allegations, which it described as "shocking" and "serious".

a3498.speaker: Bill Gates, billionaire philanthropist and chair of the Gates Foundation
a3498.speech: Has warned that growing vaccine scepticism and misinformation are fuelling preventable child deaths globally, particularly in poor countries: "It is tragic that we see this vaccine scepticism because when poor countries hear that, it spreads there as well." ; "The chance of a child dying from measles is about 30 per cent in poor countries versus one per cent in rich countries. That scepticism, which is not well-founded, will have caused more deaths outside the country than inside."

a3498.speaker: Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation
a3498.speech: Explained that vaccines have been the most significant driver of progress in reducing childhood deaths over the past five decades and linked the dramatic fall in global child mortality to vaccine access, but warned that progress is now threatened: "Well, obviously, I have been very involved with vaccines. And the biggest single reason why childhood deaths went from 10 million down to five million is because of the availability of new vaccines." ; "There were really three, one called pentavalent, one called rotavirus for diarrhoea, and one called pneumococcus for pneumonia. And those have been made available to all the world's children." ; said the cost of vaccines has been reduced "very dramatically," making room for new ones for conditions such as RSV and HPV ; "We have a great pipeline of vaccines coming."

a3498.speaker: Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation
a3498.speech: Announced a new $912 million pledge by his foundation to the Global Fund and urged the United States to sustain its leadership in financing HIV, malaria and tuberculosis programmes: "The United States has historically provided one-third of the Global Fund's total resources, largely through bipartisan support for PEPFAR and other health initiatives." ; cautioned that as Washington debates its 2025 budget, "more than half of already-approved funds remain unspent." ; "I'm optimistic that Congress will remain generous on these global health programmes," warning that cutting back now would jeopardise decades of progress against HIV, malaria and tuberculosis.

a3498.speaker: Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation
a3498.speech: Described artificial intelligence as "the biggest technological revolution" of his lifetime and said the Gates Foundation is focusing on applying AI to speed up medical discoveries, provide health advice in local languages via mobile phones, offer small farmers in Africa real-time agricultural guidance, and expand access to education: "For my work at the Gates Foundation, we have four dreams about AI. One is to use AI to discover new health tools faster than ever. The second is that if you are in a low-income country and you have a cell phone, in your native language, you should be able to talk to a virtual doctor and get advice." ; added that African farmers could soon have access to agricultural guidance "superior to what the richest farmers get today in Europe or the US."

a3498.speaker: Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation
a3498.speech: Presenting the Global Goalkeeper Award, said Spain had become "one of the most engaged donor countries in the world" under Mr Sanchez's leadership; he noted that Spain had pledged to raise its development aid to 0.7 per cent of GDP by 2030 and had more than doubled its contributions to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, since 2021, while also increasing funding to the Global Fund.

a3498.speaker: Study published in The Lancet, June 2025
a3498.speech: Found that routine vaccines have prevented about 154 million child deaths over the past five decades, but warned that slowing immunisation efforts, coupled with the spread of misinformation, could reverse hard-won progress and lead to unnecessary illness and deaths.

a3498.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a3498.speech: Has also stated that immunisation efforts are under growing threat, as misinformation, humanitarian crises, population growth, and funding cuts jeopardise routine vaccination programmes.

a3498.speaker: Muhammad Sanusi II, Emir of Kano
