a3498.speech: Described children as "the greatest trust placed in the hands of leaders" and said protecting them should be paramount; he recalled meeting a woman in 2017 who lost her child in her arms because she could not afford medication worth five dollars: "That child could have been anyone's child. The only way such societies survive is when those who have help those who do not have," adding that wealth must be seen as a divine test with gratitude expressed through generosity.

a3498.speaker: Rick Warren, American pastor
a3498.speech: Described the five million preventable child deaths recorded this year as both a humanitarian and moral crisis; drawing from his personal tragedy of losing a son to mental illness, he said, "I can't imagine five million mothers and five million fathers grieving over their children this year who should not have died. That is a moral imperative." He urged stronger collaboration between governments, businesses and faith groups: "What none of us can do by ourselves, all of us can do together."

a3498.speaker: Pedro Sanchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a3498.speech: Said Spain's approach to global health was driven by "conviction and pragmatism," recalling lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic: "There's a wrong message from Western countries that we should increase defence expenditure while reducing aid. Security is also about how we face climate change and global health."

a3498.speaker: Pedro Sanchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a3498.speech: Pushed for Palestinian statehood, saying Israel's war in Gaza had created a humanitarian tragedy: "The same values we defend in Ukraine are the same values we should defend in Palestine. I believe Israel today is less secure and more isolated than before the war."

a3504.speaker: David K. Akoi, Deputy Minister for Planning and Development, Ministry of Agriculture (Liberia)
a3504.speech: Emphasized the government's commitment to food self-sufficiency: "We are providing these machines because you've shown commitment to the Liberian Feed Yourself Agenda. Rice production is critical, and we trust these tools will help you promote sustainable farming practices and significantly reduce post-harvest losses."

a3504.speaker: Dr. Moses Zolue, RETRAP Crop Development Specialist
a3504.speech: Noted that farmers were selected based on their dedication to increasing rice production and fostering cooperative farming: "Your passion, commitment, and consistency in the area of food production, particularly rice, as well as your pledge to improve food production by reducing post-harvest losses have earned you this recognition."

a3504.speaker: Garmai Zayzay, of the Bigger Women Association of Zorzor District, Lofa County
a3504.speech: "We have been growing large quantities of rice, but processing has always been a challenge. With this equipment, we will make the Ministry's vision a reality."

a3504.speaker: Henry S. Korkoyah, head of the Kpor-gborma Agriculture Cooperative in Bong County
a3504.speech: "These machines will not only cut down on post-harvest losses but also increase our income. We are fully committed to utilizing them for the intended purpose."

a3643.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (social media post)
a3643.speech: “Elon may get more subsidy than any human being in history, by far. Perhaps we should have DOGE take a good, hard, look at this? BIG MONEY TO BE SAVED!!!”

a3643.speaker: Elon Musk (social media reply)
a3643.speech: “I am literally saying CUT IT ALL. Now.”

a3643.speaker: Elon Musk
a3643.speech: Has repeatedly criticised Trump's so-called “big, beautiful bill”, suggesting that it undermines the work he undertook to cut government spending ; has argued he is ideologically committed to cutting government spending.

a3643.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3643.speech: Has suggested that the dissent from the Tesla and SpaceX owner relates to a part of his bill that would remove incentives to buy electric vehicles, and has threatened to remove government subsidies that benefit Musk's companies ; told reporters on Tuesday morning, “He's upset that he's losing his EV mandate, he's very upset, he could lose a lot more than that, I can tell you that” ; “Doge is the monster that might have to go back and eat Elon. He gets a lot of subsidies.”

a3643.speaker: Elon Musk (posts on X)
a3643.speech: Shared a graph showing US debt over time, captioned: “When are they going to flatten this curve?” ; “Every member of Congress who campaigned on reducing government spending and then immediately voted for the biggest debt increase in history should hang their head in shame!”

a3643.speaker: Elon Musk
a3643.speech: Said he would make sure these lawmakers lost their primary races next year, and has touted the idea of establishing a new party to run against both Republicans and Democrats.

a3643.speaker: Elon Musk (reposted interview clip)
a3643.speech: Said removing EV incentives would see Tesla's “competitive position would improve significantly”.

a3646.speaker: Ambassador John Nkengasong, US Global AIDS Coordinator
a3646.speech: Says PEPFAR has invested over N$27 billion in Namibia over the past 18 years ; “PEPFAR is committed in this COPS season to invest over N$1.6 billion. I use that number to assure you that when we discuss sustainability, it is not in the light of us handing over a programme. It is in the spirit of joint responsibility and joint accountability as we move past 2030.”

a3646.speaker: Ambassador John Nkengasong, US Global AIDS Coordinator
a3646.speech: “Yesterday, at the Katutura State Hospital, I was impressed to see these women who came with us to have a dialogue, and I was honoured to have in my arms one or two of the babies that were HIV-negative, born from HIV-positive mothers who are by themselves very healthy. The smiles they had on their faces told me that they were healthy. They told me that those ladies were carrying the future of your great country in their hands.”

a3646.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services
a3646.speech: Says prior consultation with the affected governments is of the utmost necessity as donor funding for HIV is reduced ; “These programmes are an integral part of the government's developmental strategy, proper planning and implementation will ensure the continuity of activities. Any reduction in the level of external funding must be done in consultation with the ministry to allow for proper preparation.”

a3682.speaker: Richard Kumadoe, security analyst
a3682.speech: Has noted that “Justice delayed is justice denied,” pointing out how the lack of prosecutions for past violence perpetuates a dangerous cycle of impunity.

a3682.speaker: Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana) (report on the 2020 elections)
a3682.speech: Noted that victims of electoral violence are yet to receive justice despite persistent calls for investigations and speedy trials.

a3682.speaker: United States Embassy in Ghana (statement prior to the 2016 elections)
a3682.speech: Condemned all political violence and warned that it would “consider all options to hold responsible those who incite political violence, including denying or revoking visas.”

a3682.speaker: Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, former Vice President of Ghana
a3682.speech: Has condemned the violence, warning that normalizing it would put the country on a dangerous path ; “This will be a recipe for disaster if each political party will raise its own army”; he urged President John Mahama to ensure swift accountability for the perpetrators.

a3682.speaker: Sam George, NDC Minister of Communication
a3682.speech: “Someone should tell Bawumia to shut up. What did he say about Ayawaso West Wuogon in 2019?”

a3682.speaker: Minority Caucus in Parliament, led by Alexander Afenyo-Markin
a3682.speech: Strongly accused the opposition NDC of orchestrating the violence, specifically naming Malik Basintale and Mustapha Gbande as instigators; their statement asserted that such actions are “a direct attack on our democratic process,” depriving citizens of their constitutional right to representation.

a3682.speaker: Dr Hannah Louisa Bissiw, Administrator of the Minerals Development Fund
a3682.speech: Claimed she was a past victim of political violence allegedly orchestrated by Madam Koomson during the Ayawaso West Wuogon by-election: “She came with about 30 thugs to me, I was beaten.”

a3682.speaker: Afrobarometer surveys
a3682.speech: Show a decline in public confidence in the Electoral Commission, hitting its lowest level in over two decades; while a majority (64%) believed the 2020 election was generally free and fair, this was a significant drop from 2016 (87%).

a3682.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) and the International Federation of Journalists (IFJ)
a3682.speech: Have documented multiple attacks on journalists in Ghana, particularly during elections.

a3682.speaker: Ghana Journalists Association (GJA)
a3682.speech: Has consistently called for perpetrators to be prosecuted and has even released media blacklists against politicians who assault media workers.

a3682.speaker: Albert Kwabena Dwumfour, GJA President
a3682.speech: Has expressed concern about the slow pace of investigations into the murder of journalist Ahmed Suale, who was shot dead in 2019; signaled that the GJA may seek redress in international forums like the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice if no concrete progress is made.

a3682.speaker: A study on electoral violence in the Tamale metropolis
a3682.speech: Discovered multifaceted root causes, with poverty being a leading factor, representing 34.8%; confirmed that election-related violence has significant effects, including maiming, deaths, and destruction of property, and called for a comprehensive, multi-stakeholder approach to address the problem.

a3847.speaker: Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (communique)
a3847.speech: According to a communique from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the suspension of USAID funds is justified by the same arguments brandished by Donald Trump's supporters, namely the presumptions of covert financing of terrorism ; According to the same communique, the transition authorities even claim an anticipatory posture in this matter, with an alleged refusal to grant the no-objection notice to the financing of all USAID projects that were reluctant to pass through the state channel.

a3871.speaker: Lesley Mkandawire, economist
a3871.speech: “The economy is doing badly. Prices of goods are rising rapidly, and it is everyone’s expectation that the next budget should bring recovery.”

a3871.speaker: World Bank Malawi Economic Monitor (report)
a3871.speech: Highlighted this worrying trend, noting that while overall spending was 14.2 percent below target, crucial sectors such as public sector wages continued to spiral out of control. “With liquidity constraints in the domestic securities market, the government had to scale down domestically financed projects to accommodate wage bill increases,” the report observed.

a3871.speaker: Bertha Bangala Chikadza, President of the Economics Association of Malawi
a3871.speech: Emphasises that investment in productive sectors is the only way to spur long-term economic recovery: “The budget should be in line with MIP-1. We need production, so productive sectors need serious investments.”

a3871.speaker: Thomas Munthali, Director General of the National Planning Commission
a3871.speech: Argues that sustainable revenue generation—not reliance on borrowing—is the key to economic stability: “If we are relying on borrowing and resources from external partners, it is not going to work. It’s high time we developed internal capacity for revenue generation and mobilization for sustainable development.”

a3871.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Malawi Finance Minister
a3871.speech: Has hinted at efforts to cut the deficit while increasing production-related spending.

a4209.speaker: Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN) (filing and statement to the ICC)
a4209.speech: Announced that it had submitted a 172-page document to ICC prosecutor Karim Khan detailing how Biden, Blinken and Austin provided military, political and public support to Israel, including arms transfers worth $17.9 billion, intelligence sharing, targeting assistance and diplomatic protection; DAWN’s statement asserts that Biden, Blinken and Austin are guilty of complicity in Israeli crimes, in violation of articles 25(3)(c) and (d) of the Rome Statute, including war crimes such as starvation and the bombing of civilians and crimes against humanity such as murder and persecution, and also raises involvement in genocide; DAWN maintains that Trump’s executive order sanctioning ICC officials could expose him to charges of obstruction of justice under article 70 of the Rome Statute, and says Biden’s actions contributed to starvation-related crimes by depriving Palestinians of humanitarian aid.

a4209.speaker: Reed Brody, DAWN board member and war crimes lawyer
a4209.speech: “The complicity of Biden, Blinken and Austin in Israel’s crimes can legitimately be investigated” ; “The bombs dropped on Palestinian hospitals, schools and homes are American bombs, thanks to the support of the United States. American officials knew what was happening, but they never stopped their aid.”

a4209.speaker: Sarah Leah Whitson, executive director of DAWN
a4209.speech: Condemned the actions of the American officials: “They disregarded overwhelming evidence of Israel’s crimes, rejected staff recommendations to end arms transfers and reinforced their unconditional support. They allowed Israel to continue its atrocities.”

a4209.speaker: Raed Jarrar, DAWN’s advocacy director
a4209.speech: “Trump is not just obstructing justice: he is trying to destroy the courthouse to prevent those responsible from being held to account. His forced displacement plan should also be the subject of an investigation.”

a4276.speaker: Moussa Aden Miganeh, prefect of the Ali-Sabieh region
a4276.speech: Welcomed her to the capital of his region, Ali-Sabieh town, and spoke briefly with her.

a4276.speaker: Omar Ahmed Wais, president of the regional council of Ali-Sabieh
a4276.speech: "We greet you, Madam Minister of Youth and Culture, you and the members of your delegation. We welcome you to the beautiful town of Ali-Sabieh. This is her second visit to our regional capital, which means making contact with the regional officials and the spokespeople of the population. Your Excellency, Madam Minister, be welcome in the town of Aska and at the headquarters of the regional decentralisation body. We will work with you and get to know you well."

a4276.speaker: Active women of civil society in Ali-Sabieh
a4276.speech: Welcomed the guest of the day and her companions to Ali-Sabieh; a good welcome is a tradition among us, they said.

a4276.speaker: Abdi Khaireh Bouh, member of the National Assembly
a4276.speech: Stressed that linking youth with culture obliges us to teach them our ancestral traditions.

a4276.speaker: Moussa Aden Miganeh, prefect of the Ali-Sabieh region
a4276.speech: Declared that the Assajog craftswomen have done much to preserve the useful objects of the national cultural tradition; every year they organise their own exhibition fair, and "We help them intensively so that they can live from their production."

a4276.speaker: Lloyd Jackson, USAID representative in Djibouti
a4276.speech: Assured that his agency stands ready to support and finance all the projects of the Ministry of Youth and Culture deemed important.

a4276.speaker: Dr Hibo Moumin Assoweh, Minister of Youth and Culture
a4276.speech: Thanked the regional authorities and the civil society leaders for their warm welcome. "For us, getting to know the spokespeople of the population with whom we will later be expected to work in the framework of our mission is essential. The remarkable presence of women in the hall shows that they are respected in the region. Working with young people to strengthen their knowledge and practices regarding national cultural traditions remains one of our ministerial department's priorities. Also enabling them to succeed in their socio-economic integration into life," she declared.

a4276.speaker: Aicha Hassan Nouho, head of the Community Development Centre of Ali-Sabieh
a4276.speech: Introduced them to the centre's various sections - library, games rooms, rooms for learning folk dances - and explained to her interlocutors the function of each corner of the place.

a4276.speaker: Chaban Daher Moussa, sub-prefect of the sector, the village chief and other representatives of the population at Assamo
A young woman speaking for the youth of Assamo village
a4276.speech: Requested from the minister, in addition to the CDC, the construction of a cultural training centre as well as a sports field.

a4276.speaker: Dr Hibo Moumin Assoweh, Minister of Youth and Culture
a4276.speech: Responded favourably to their requests, while stressing everyone's contribution to the community development of Assamo, which remains a locality rich in potential in culture, agriculture and agro-pastoral industry.

a4276.speaker: Ismael Guedi Waberi, head of the Daasbiyo Community Development Centre, and representatives of the village's inhabitants
a4276.speech: Delivered the welcome address and took the microphone one after the other to thank the minister for her visit and the equipment offered; they conveyed their grievances and submitted the need for a regular maintenance service for their CDC.

a4276.speaker: Moussa Aden Miganeh, prefect of the Ali-Sabieh region
a4276.speech: Recalled, emphasising the social infrastructure projects developed in the locality; also stressed the importance of the construction of the road section linking Daasbiyo to the regional capital, a road whose tarring project is under study and which will certainly make Daasbiyo the most visited village in the country thanks to its thousand-year-old cultural remains, saying the development of tourism will benefit greatly from it and will allow the creation of a multitude of youth integration projects and other activities.

a4276.speaker: Dr Hibo Moumin Assoweh, Minister of Youth and Culture
a4276.speech: Thanked the population for the fraternal and warm welcome given to her and her companions, and recalled the change of status of the CDCs, formerly called youth and culture houses, which currently play an important role in community development and which must be the gathering places of the locality's inhabitants.

a4353.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a4353.speech: "It is a mark of love and friendship in that the amount of the second compact exceeds the first," comments Boni Yayi, who calls it a first in the MCC partnership ; for him, democracy must rest on three essential pillars, namely strong, credible institutions managed by quality people, and freedom, which presupposes the security of persons, goods and capital, the last pillar concerning infrastructure, which puts the energy question at the heart of the stakes of prosperity.

a4353.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a4353.speech: Indicates that the exclusive orientation of the American financing towards the energy sector comes at just the right time to bring about a qualitative transformation of the Beninese economy ; "The reforms will make it possible to support the regulatory authority, questions of pricing, to open the sector to private players, with legal documents supporting public-private partnership," he insists ; confides that the expected investments should allow the installation of a capacity of about 78 MW, more than half of which devoted to renewable energy.

a4353.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a4353.speech: Reassured his interlocutor of the dispatch of 800 Beninese soldiers to reinforce the ranks of the multinational force being created to defeat the Islamic State in West Africa ; requested the logistical and financial support of the United States so that the mission assigned to this force may be successfully accomplished within a short time.

a4353.speaker: Joe Biden, Vice-President of the United States of America
a4353.speech: "The second compact is not automatic. This compact is a consequence of your personal leadership, which has made an enormous difference," maintains Joe Biden, who welcomes the fact that the USA is strengthening its partnership with a country that is exemplary in matters of democracy and freedoms ; "Africa is a continent full of youthful energy and promise. We must focus, create opportunities for that energy, and give young people promises," he stresses.

a4353.speaker: Joe Biden, Vice-President of the United States of America
a4353.speech: Indicates that the American program helped to double the capacity of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, while acknowledging that many challenges remain to be met, including energy ; according to him this second MCA compact constitutes the largest MCC investment in the energy sector and the most important American support in the renewable energy sub-sector ; affirms that MCA 2 will impact the entire Beninese population in terms of access to electricity and will help to better manage public resources and promote private investment ; "Obama's objective is to ensure energy for Africa, not only through the MCC but all the vehicles to be mobilised to bring light to all the regions of the continent. We are delighted to renew this partnership thanks to your commitment to democracy, good governance and the fight against corruption," he concludes.

a4353.speaker: Joe Biden, Vice-President of the United States of America
a4353.speech: Hailed the leadership shown by Boni Yayi in mobilising the international community against the terrorist peril in the Sahel-Saharan belt and his fight alongside the countries of the Lake Chad Basin Commission to put an end to the abuses of the Boko Haram Islamist sect ; his priority today is the restoration of security in the West African sub-region, in particular the merciless fight against the Boko Haram Islamist sect.

a4356.speaker: Suhail Shaheen, head of the Taliban political office in Doha
a4356.speech: Said the meeting, whose agenda was negotiated for months between the UN and the fundamentalists, will address the fight against narcotics and financial and banking sanctions.

a4356.speaker: Zabiullah Mujahid, chief spokesman of the Kabul government (Taliban)
a4356.speech: Replied today during a press conference, when asked why representatives of Afghan women had not been invited: "The Afghan Islamic Emirate is the government of Afghanistan and there should be no other representatives of Afghanistan" ; stated that "issues related to Afghans are internal issues and international meetings are not the appropriate place to raise them."

a4356.speaker: Taliban (fundamentalist government)
a4356.speech: According to the fundamentalist government, giving Afghans a voice through different channels "opens the way to foreign interference."

a4356.speaker: Afghan women's rights activists
a4356.speech: Expressed their disappointment with the meeting which, in their view, has no relevance if fundamental rights issues are not addressed.

a4356.speaker: Mina Rafiq, Afghan rights defender, speaking to EFE
a4356.speech: "The most important and catastrophic issue is that of the rights of Afghan women, which are completely ignored by the Taliban. If the meeting is a UN meeting and has no political interests, women should and must be part of the meeting" ; lamented that without this "the meeting will open the way to further violations of the rights of Afghan women and their deprivation of public life and, once again, their rights will be ignored."

a4365.speaker: Mark Toner, United States Ambassador to Liberia
a4365.speech: Expressed hope for the renewal of Executive Order No. 131 creating the Office for the Establishment of War and Economic Crimes Court for Liberia, and acknowledged the inadequate funding allotted for the implementation of OWECC-L mandates; said President Joseph Nyumah Boakai doing more for the OWECC-L would further demonstrate his commitment to his campaign promises; pledged the US mission’s continuous engagement and advocacy with his government for the full fulfillment of OWECC-L’s mandate ; “While the advocacy and engagement are ongoing, the Liberian government should convince the international community why Liberia needs a war crimes court.”

a4365.speaker: Dr. Cllr. Jallah A. Barbu, Executive Director of the Office for the Establishment of War and Economic Crimes Court for Liberia (OWECC-L)
a4365.speech: Described the Ambassador’s visit as a sign of goodwill toward Liberia’s peace process; highlighted the severe challenges in securing government funding for operations, which has demotivated his staff who have not been paid for the past three months; said a lot of progress has been made in outreach, producing roadmap and framework documents, and working with civil society organizations ; “We are not discouraged but not happy with the trend, and despite these administrative challenges, the staff are tremendously making progress toward archiving OWECC-L’s mandates.” ; “The Office extends its gratitude to the U.S. Embassy for this meaningful engagement and looks forward to continued collaboration in the spirit of justice and national healing.”

a4633.speaker: UNICEF-Malawi (report on the situation of children in Malawi-2024)
a4633.speech: Applauds the Malawi Government as its strategic development partner, alongside other stakeholder donors, for the critical role they played in achieving significant results and progress for children in Malawi in 2024; indicates that government spending on essential services increased in 2023 to 2024 from 29.3% to 31%, on health including WASH from 10% to 12.6%, and social protection from 3% to 3.7%, while education was the only social sector in which government support did not increase, decreasing from 15.7% to 14.8%.

a4633.speaker: UNICEF-Malawi (report on the situation of children in Malawi-2024)
a4633.speech: Acknowledges that "Malawi's macro-fiscal challenges - including unsustainable debt, foreign exchange shortages and inflation - threatened social sector investments" ; "Consequently, UNICEF advocated for protecting social sector spending and mobilizing resources. Strategic partnerships with the government and civil society organisations (CSOs) drove reforms and secured funding for inclusive social protection systems."

a4633.speaker: UNICEF-Malawi (report on the situation of children in Malawi-2024)
a4633.speech: Takes cognizance that government's evaluations of programmes like the social cash transfer programme (SCTP) led to improved designs and expanded coverage following the 2023-2024 El Nino-induced drought that left over 5.7 million people facing acute food insecurity; reports that through the SCTP over 2.5 million people were reached with integrated life-saving services. "The adverse conditions [of El Nino-induced drought] widened existing nutrition gaps and disproportionately affected individuals with chronic illnesses such as HIV and tuberculosis, whose dietary needs were often unmet. The effects of El Nino underscored the urgent need to integrate climate resilience into Malawi's development agenda and UNICEF continued its key role in inter-agency emergency preparedness and response coordination."

a4633.speaker: UNICEF-Malawi (report on the situation of children in Malawi-2024)
a4633.speech: Reports that shortly after the Government established the National Children's Commission (NCC) and submitted its report to the Committee on the Rights of the Child, the agency operationalised its Secretariat, supported the NCC's structure, contributed to its annual work plan and raised awareness nationwide, and continued to advocate for increased and sustained government investment in adolescent health and maternal and newborn health services: "These efforts were driven through strategic, high-level engagements, including direct dialogue with the Minister of Health and active participation in key multi-stakeholder platforms convened by the Ministry."

a4633.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a4633.speech: Pledged at the launch of the Malawi Congress Party manifesto that once given the mandate for a second term his administration shall introduce future bank accounts for every newborn child, where the government will deposit K500,000 accessible when they turn 18. "This is how we build a Malawi where poverty is not inherited" ; "This new five-pillar manifesto aims to transform Malawi by 2030, beginning with eradicating hunger through comprehensive agricultural reforms that will ensure sustainable food security for every citizen."

a4633.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a4633.speech: Highlighted that some initiatives pledged ahead of the 2020 fresh elections - including the 1 million jobs - stalled due to global and domestic challenges, but emphasised that progress had still been made in critical areas like infrastructure, health, and housing. "Despite the storms we've faced, including CoVID-19, global economic shocks, Cyclone Ana & Freddy, cholera outbreak - and the Chikangawa tragedy that claimed the life of Vice-President Saulos Klaus Chilima, we have laid a solid foundation. With your trust, we will finish the job."

a4633.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a4633.speech: On his campaign trail, pledges to govern with transparency, vision, and results if re-elected, adding that the manifesto's five core pillars are food security; job and wealth creation; governance; reform; and rebooting public service delivery; described the youth as "the engine of national progress".

a4801.speaker: Algerian Ministry of National Defence
a4801.speech: According to it, the aid comprises foodstuffs, medicines, medical supplies, tents and mattresses; it was provided by the Algerian Red Crescent to the State of Niger and arrived from the Boufarik air base, in the First Military Region, at Niamey airport in Niger.

a4875.speaker: Gaza's civil defence agency
a4875.speech: Said Israeli forces killed another 21 people waiting for aid in the Palestinian territory yesterday.

a4875.speaker: Mahmud Bassal, Gaza civil defence spokesman
a4875.speech: Told AFP that 21 people were killed and around 150 wounded "as a result of the Israeli occupation forces' targeting of gatherings of citizens waiting for aid... in the central Gaza Strip with bullets and tank shells" in the early hours yesterday.

a4875.speaker: Rabhi al-Qassas, eyewitness
a4875.speech: "How long will this situation go on? How long will people have to endure this? We want a solution for these victims who are dying," he told AFP.

a4875.speaker: Israeli military
a4875.speech: Said that a gathering overnight had been identified in an area "adjacent" to its troops in the Netzarim corridor in central Gaza, where the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) aid group is known to hand out food ; said reports of individuals injured by military fire in the area were "under review."

a4875.speaker: Rights groups
a4875.speech: According to rights groups, the Gaza population of more than two million is suffering famine-like conditions after an Israeli blockade.

a4875.speaker: United Nations
a4875.speech: Condemned the "weaponisation of food" in Gaza as a war crime and urged Israel's military to "stop shooting at people trying to get food."

a4875.speaker: UN human rights office (written notes provided before a briefing)
a4875.speech: "Israel's militarised humanitarian assistance mechanism is in contradiction with international standards on aid distribution."

a4875.speaker: UN agencies and major aid groups
a4875.speech: Have refused to cooperate with GHF over concerns it was designed to cater to Israeli military objectives.

a4875.speaker: Health ministry in the Hamas-run Gaza Strip (figures issued on Saturday)
a4875.speech: According to figures issued on Saturday, at least 450 people have been killed and nearly 3,500 injured by Israeli fire while seeking aid since late May.

a4875.speaker: Rescuers
a4875.speech: According to rescuers, many of those killed have been near sites operated by the GHF.

a4875.speaker: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF)
a4875.speech: Says some deadly incidents have occurred near UN convoys.

a4988.speaker: UN refugee agency
a4988.speech: According to the UN refugee agency, the number of people displaced by armed conflict in Somalia amounts to 3 million.

a4988.speaker: Ayan Ali Hussein, chairwoman of the Dooxdoox IDP camp on the outskirts of Mogadishu
a4988.speech: said Trump's order provoked almost immediate stop-work orders addressed to USAID partners, shutting down basic services: "there are no facilities to treat malnourished children" ; "Women who had experienced gender-based violence once had access to care, counseling, protection, medication, financial support, and clothing, none of which are available anymore" ; said her camp looks after eight sites, home to nearly 8,000 households of internally displaced Somalis who will "lack basic items like plastic sheets" for temporary shelter ; said the suspension of USAID "left a huge void in our lives".

a4988.speaker: Ruqiya Abdulle Ubeyd, 85-year-old mother of eight and camp resident
a4988.speech: said she was shocked by Trump's decision and asked "the U.S. government to restore the aid it used to give to vulnerable people".

a4988.speaker: Dr. Abdiqani Sheikh Omar, founder of the Somali Young Doctors Association (SOYDA) and previously a top official in Somalia's health ministry
a4988.speech: said the abruptness of Trump's announcement has destabilized their programs ; said that in 2025 Somalia was to receive $125 million in USAID support for programs that could now become "null and void" ; said that to cope with funding shortages his group decided to prioritize critical nutrition and hygiene programs, and that with many workers facing immediate job losses the organization is "engaging our volunteer health professionals to cover this emergency staff funding gap through part-time shifts".

a4988.speaker: Hussein Abikar, father of five living in the camp
a4988.speech: "Previously, whenever our children got sick, we would come straight to (the SODYA) center for help" ; "There is no other place where we could find such support."

a5142.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
a5142.speech: have sharply criticized South African President Cyril Ramaphosa for allegedly breaching diplomatic protocols after contacting billionaire Elon Musk regarding the recently enacted Expropriation Act. The EFF labeled Ramaphosa’s actions as “reckless,” accusing him of compromising South Africa’s sovereignty to appease U.S. interests ; expressed dismay over Ramaphosa’s direct engagement with Musk—an unelected U.S. business figure—highlighting concerns over the President’s willingness to prioritize foreign business interests over national policy integrity. “This breaking of diplomatic protocol should never be taken lightly,” the statement read, describing it as symptomatic of a “dependency syndrome” on Western influence.

a5142.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
a5142.speech: accused Musk of exploiting his ties with former U.S. President Donald Trump to pressure South African authorities into easing regulatory barriers for his satellite company, Starlink. According to the EFF, Musk’s push undermines South Africa’s Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (B-BBEE) policy, which mandates that foreign-owned satellite firms allocate at least 30% ownership to historically disadvantaged South Africans.

a5142.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
a5142.speech: criticized Ramaphosa’s inconsistency, noting that just days earlier, the government reprimanded Minister Gwede Mantashe for diplomatic missteps when he threatened to restrict mineral exports to the U.S. over foreign aid disputes.

a5142.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement)
a5142.speech: “The President’s conduct risks opening the door to state capture,” the EFF warned, drawing parallels to South Africa’s troubled past with the Gupta family during Jacob Zuma’s administration. The party urged Ramaphosa to avoid relying on foreign billionaires to shape national policy, stressing the importance of upholding diplomatic protocols and protecting South Africa’s sovereignty.

a5142.speaker: Gwede Mantashe, South African Minister of Mineral Resources
a5142.speech: threatened to restrict mineral exports to the U.S. over foreign aid disputes.

a5398.speaker: UNCTAD's Economic Development in Africa Report 2020, "Tackling illicit financial flows for sustainable development in Africa"
a5398.speech: Estimates that every year $88.6 billion, equivalent to 3.7% of Africa's GDP, leaves the continent as illicit capital flight, nearly as much as the combined total annual inflows of official development assistance ($48 billion) and foreign direct investment ($54 billion); that from 2000 to 2015 total illicit capital flight amounted to $836 billion, making Africa a "net creditor to the world"; that in African countries with high IFFs governments spend 25% less on health and 58% less on education than countries with low IFFs; that tackling capital flight and IFFs represents a large potential source of capital to finance investment; that in Sierra Leone curbing capital flight and investing a constant share of revenues in public health could save an additional 2,322 of the 258,000 children born annually; and that curbing illicit capital flight could generate enough capital by 2030 to finance almost 50% of the $2.4 trillion needed by sub-Saharan African countries for climate change adaptation and mitigation.

a5398.speaker: Mukhisa Kituyi, UNCTAD Secretary-General
a5398.speech: "Illicit financial flows rob Africa and its people of their prospects, undermining transparency and accountability and eroding trust in African institutions."

a5566.speaker: Sarah Abdelazem Hassana, Deputy Minister of Health of Sudan
a5566.speech: Welcomed "the swift action taken by all IGAD Heads of State and Government to contain and fight the spread of the Corona virus"; on behalf of the Minister of Health of Sudan and chair of the IGAD ministerial health committee, Dr Akram Ali Eltom, she conveyed Sudan's commitment to mobilise national resources in the fight against the Corona virus; she urged the IGAD Secretariat to speed up the process of deploying response teams in member states and to facilitate a coordinated partnership.

a5566.speaker: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of IGAD
a5566.speech: Recalled that the main objective of the meeting was to discuss the current needs of member states, to fight the coronavirus collaboratively and to provide projections of the infrastructural, technical and material capacities urgently needed for the duration of the epidemic, through a response strategy to fight COVID-19; he also reiterated his call for protection from the pandemic for vulnerable populations such as displaced persons, refugees and migrants in the region.

a5566.speaker: Dr Workneh Gebeyehu, Executive Secretary of IGAD
a5566.speech: Highlighted the serious disruption of "livelihoods, social and economic security" for the region's 270 million people that the disease could cause ; "If we do not act quickly to stop it and minimise its impact, the virus has the potential to turn into a social and economic catastrophe," said Dr Workneh before presenting a draft call to action for deliberation and adoption.

a5566.speaker: IGAD health ministers
a5566.speech: Discussed, on the guiding principle that "no country is safe until every country is safe", ways of operationalising the outcomes of the 30 March IGAD summit, including the development of an IGAD regional response strategy for COVID-19, the creation of an emergency fund for COVID-19 and other disease outbreaks and the strengthening of national response systems; they approved the outlines of a regional response plan (RRP) presented by the IGAD Secretariat and created a regional expert working group to coordinate and monitor the regional response, and issued a call-to-action document at the end of the meeting.

a5566.speaker: Ibrahim Elbadawi, Minister of Finance of Sudan
a5566.speech: Expressed his own and his country's determination to ensure that "COVID-19 does not translate into a recession curve" for the region and its people; he stressed that the IGAD region "cannot afford to be complacent" in the face of the current threat; he welcomed the initiative of a regional response in the context of promoting cooperation and ensuring that work is carried out not only at country level but also on a regional basis to mitigate the potential fallout and impact of COVID-19 on the region's economies.

a5566.speaker: Jutta Urpilainen, European Union Commissioner for International Partnerships
a5566.speech: Welcomed the fact that IGAD had held a summit, a meeting of health ministers and a meeting of finance ministers when she joined the conversation; the Commissioner announced the establishment of an EU financial package comprising "immediate humanitarian aid" and "support for strengthening health systems and mitigating the economic crisis."

a5882.speaker: Western intelligence services
a5882.speech: According to Western intelligence services, the chemical attack in Damascus caused the death of 1,300 people.

a5882.speaker: Parliamentarians of the UMP, the left radicals, the Left Front and the UDI (France)
a5882.speech: Criticised Prime Minister Jean-Marc Ayrault and demanded proof from the UN that the attack was orchestrated by Bashar Al-Assad.

a5882.speaker: Lucien Pambou, municipal councillor (UMP)
a5882.speech: "There is a problem that Obama does not mention, and Hollande even less: Bashar's departure could leave a significant vacuum by creating an ethnic-religious war, which is already visible between Sunnis and Shias, and even accelerate the coming to power of Islamist jihadists, which neither France, nor the United States, and still less Israel, wants."

a5882.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a5882.speech: In an exclusive interview granted to the AP agency and the Perviy Kanal channel, affirmed that Russia would be ready to act resolutely, and even to support armed action by Western countries, but that Russian support would only be granted on condition that the evidence establishing the use of chemical weapons in Syria be convincing and that the UN give its green light.

a5980.speaker: Presidential decree of Nicaragua (text presented by co-presidents Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo)
a5980.speech: According to the presidential text, the objective of the measure is to "allow exchanges and mutually beneficial humanitarian assistance, in the event of emergencies", during the second half of next year.

a6077.speaker: Bihi Iman Egeh, Minister of Finance of the Federal Government of Somalia
a6077.speech: “I thank the U.S. government and people for their unwavering support of our economic reforms and growth.”

a6155.speaker: Alphonce Kalula, Advisory Officer of the USAID maternal and child health project
a6155.speech: Said the strategy stems from the challenges they identified regarding the availability of competency-based training for students in that sector who are in colleges ; "We want to invest in students so that even if they are employed today they are able to work serving pregnant women in hospitals, because they have the capability, in order to reduce maternal and child deaths" ; He said the plan is to reach 200 students in each college every year, who will benefit from the use of this equipment ; "We have started here at Muhimbili; we have brought them equipment that resembles the reality of the environment, such as equipment for helping a mother to give birth and for carrying out examinations."

a6155.speaker: Redemptha Matindi, Director of Nursing and Midwifery Services at Muhimbili National Hospital
a6155.speech: Said the equipment will bring efficiency and confidence by preparing the student to deliver quality services ; "Health care requires more preparation of the student through practical study; we have been seeing education being provided and people acquiring skills, and it has been a great help to the student when they come to meet a real patient having already acquired the knowledge" ; Said that where the world is heading there are major technological changes and the community is striving to know its rights because it is reached by a great deal of information ; "Coming with practical study reduces complaints from those who receive services, but for a student who is studying in order to obtain a certificate, practical and theoretical education must go together."

a6155.speaker: Rozi Mgonja, Head of the Nursing and Midwifery Department
a6155.speech: Said they received the equipment with joy because the need for it is great ; "This equipment is good and sturdy; it will help us teach students in the practical learning laboratory, and if they pass here they will go on to meet patients in the wards. It is a good thing; it means the student does not go straight to a patient, and it makes them practise many times so that when they reach a patient they can serve them more professionally" ; She said the equipment they were given helps in assisting a pregnant woman to give birth and in family planning, as well as in examining mothers, explaining that other items will be used for carrying out examinations.

a6155.speaker: Maridhawa Jaji, teacher and instructor at the college
a6155.speech: Said the equipment was delivered at the right time because they need more to teach students practically. She said the mannequins will help them teach the student the best way to deliver a pregnant woman and to carry out examinations practically.

a6155.speaker: Fridas Ally, third-year nursing and midwifery student at MUHAS
a6155.speech: Said the equipment will increase their skills while they are in class. "It is equipment that relates mostly to family planning matters and to the best way of giving birth; we promise we will use it well and bring the required benefit by serving patients after finishing our studies."

a6173.speaker: Patrick Pouyanné, TotalEnergies CEO
a6173.speech: In July expressed confidence, as quoted in a Bloomberg report, that Namibia would experience an oil boom similar to Guyana’s.

a6173.speaker: OilNOW (online news platform)
a6173.speech: Noted that Bloomberg had quoted Maggy Shino, Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner.

a6173.speaker: Maggy Shino, Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner
a6173.speech: “We are preparing the country to be an energy hub for the region.”

a6173.speaker: Bloomberg
a6173.speech: Reported Namibia’s economy could potentially double or triple by 2027.

a6173.speaker: Maggy Shino, Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner
a6173.speech: Quoted in a recent Reuters report explaining that government is collaborating with operators, including Shell, TotalEnergies and Galp, to design a shared infrastructure plan that may involve an upscale version of the Kudu gas-to-power project.

a6173.speaker: Patrick Pouyanné, TotalEnergies CEO
a6173.speech: Indicated that achieving acceptable production costs is challenging, amid difficulties related to the high costs of reinjecting gas.

a6173.speaker: Wael Sawan, Shell CEO
a6173.speech: Told analysts last month that Namibia’s acreage is “very challenging” and that the lower permeability of the rock made extracting oil and gas harder ; “A lot of our focus is on figuring out whether we can find ways to be able to develop commercially investable projects.”

a6229.speaker: Dr. Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of the Jospong Group of Companies
a6229.speech: Has said Ghana and Africa has a lot to gain from their relationship with South Korea in terms of business and development ; "Opportunity is important in business," he said, adding, "South Korea has advanced technology in renewable energies such as solar and wind power which can benefit our continent." ; "South Korea has capacity that can benefit African businesses and they need to unleash that to benefit the continent and Ghana," he said, adding "The Private sector is ready to partner Korea which must remove restrictions and bureaucracy as it seeks to support 48 African nations."

a6229.speaker: Dr. Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of the Jospong Group of Companies
a6229.speech: Commended South Korean President Yoon Suk-Yeol for his commitment to boosting support for Africa, including enhanced trade and investment pledges.

a6229.speaker: Dr. Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of the Jospong Group of Companies
a6229.speech: "The whole world is about climate change," Dr. Agyepong said, adding, "In Ghana Jospong Group has tackled waste management as a serious issue, from collection, haulage, composting, recycling and other forms of treatments."

a6229.speaker: Dr. Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of the Jospong Group of Companies
a6229.speech: Further stressed the need for collaboration in critical areas like minerals, digital transformation, climate change, food security, and public health.

a6229.speaker: Dr. Joseph Siaw Agyepong, Executive Chairman of the Jospong Group of Companies
a6229.speech: Was optimistic about the future of Korea-Africa relations, stating, "The future looks bright, and I'm thrilled to be part of this transformative journey."

a6229.speaker: South Korea (announcement at the Korea-Africa Summit)
a6229.speech: Announced plans to increase official development assistance to $10 billion by 2030 and provide $14 billion in export financing.

a6304.speaker: Donald Trump, US presidential candidate / former President
a6304.speech: Has pledged to make the United States the "bitcoin and cryptocurrency capital of the world" and to put tech billionaire Elon Musk in charge of a wide-ranging audit of governmental waste.

a6304.speaker: US media
a6304.speech: Have thus far projected that Trump has won in 24 states, including big prizes Texas and Ohio, key battlegrounds Georgia and North Carolina and other reliably Republican-leaning states.

a6304.speaker: Russ Mould, analyst at AJ Bell
a6304.speech: "The price of bitcoin has closely followed Trump's position in the polls and on betting markets" ; investors are "potentially taking the view that a Republican victory would lead to a surge in demand for the digital currency," he added.

a6304.speaker: Analysts
a6304.speech: Said attention was also on Congressional races, adding that a clean sweep for Trump and Republicans would likely boost the dollar and Treasury yields owing to his plans to cut taxes and impose tariffs on imports.

a6304.speaker: Stephen Innes, SPI Asset Management
a6304.speech: Said Republican control of the Senate and House "could bring sweeping spending or tax policy shifts. Still, congressional gridlock could be the ultimate volatility suppressor."

a6304.speaker: Donald Trump, US presidential candidate / former President
a6304.speech: Vowed to ratchet up a trade battle with China by imposing massive tariffs on goods from the country.

a6324.speaker: Luísa Meque, chairperson of the National Disaster Management Institute (INGD), Mozambique's relief agency
a6324.speech: Announced on Wednesday that at least 1,863 families were affected by Jude and 908 houses were completely destroyed: "From the preliminary survey carried out, we have six deaths, one in Larde district, another in Meconta district and four in Nacala Port. These are the deaths confirmed by the health authorities. There are twenty injured. This is preliminary data and the teams are still working on the ground. This information will be updated and may change in the next few hours."

a6324.speaker: Luísa Meque, chairperson of the National Disaster Management Institute (INGD), Mozambique's relief agency
a6324.speech: Speaking during a session of the Emergency Operations Centre (COE) in Nampula city, said humanitarian assistance for the communities and households affected by Jude is raising concerns due to the condition of the roads: "The rain that accompanied 'Jude' caused many access routes to be cut and rivers to burst their banks, flooding various regions. This is a major challenge, therefore we call on the people who are besieged by the rising waters to avoid crossing the rivers. It's important that they don't cross without safety, because that could endanger their lives."

a6324.speaker: Luísa Meque, chairperson of the National Disaster Management Institute (INGD), Mozambique's relief agency
a6324.speech: "The frequent occurrence of cyclones in this part of the country, going beyond the meteorological forecasts, is a factor that increases the pressure on the government to provide humanitarian assistance to households, a reality that must be lived with."

a6324.speaker: Zambezia maritime authorities
a6324.speech: Have ordered all fishermen not to take their boats to sea.

a6391.speaker: The National Interest (British newspaper article)
a6391.speech: Reported that, unlike Washington, which centralised its aid through USAID, Moscow relies on a more flexible and multipolar model, mobilising more than a dozen ministries and public organisations, and that these entities run various programmes in the fields of development, culture, education and humanitarian assistance in the event of disaster.

a6391.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6391.speech: Estimate that Russia's annual aid reached more than one billion dollars before the war in Ukraine.

a6391.speaker: Evgeny Primakov, Director of the Rossotrudnichestvo agency (Russian Cooperation)
a6391.speech: In an interview, gave an overview of Russia's future foreign aid apparatus, indicating that the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs is preparing a new architecture for foreign aid, inspired by the USAID model but adapted to Russian realities, with the aim of grouping efforts under a structured entity and of increasing its funding.

a6391.speaker: Evgeny Primakov, Director of the Rossotrudnichestvo agency (Russian Cooperation)
a6391.speech: Acknowledged that, in a context marked by a costly war, priorities are being readjusted, but nevertheless insisted on the need to target concrete and measurable socio-political results, stressing that foreign aid must serve the country's interests — not as a simple act of charity, but as a strategic, win-win lever.

a6391.speaker: Evgeny Primakov, Director of the Rossotrudnichestvo agency (Russian Cooperation)
a6391.speech: Also mentioned competition with China in certain areas, notably in the matter of student scholarships ; “For now, we hope to be able to compete with a country like Finland,” he indicated.

a6391.speaker: Certain Western media (unnamed)
a6391.speech: Have attempted to discredit Rossotrudnichestvo's activities by accusing it of serving as a front for propaganda and intelligence operations.

a6391.speaker: European Union
a6391.speech: Sanctioned the agency in 2022, because of what it claims was the launch of a network of “agents of influence” to mobilise support for the war in Ukraine.

a6513.speaker: Sidi Ould Tah, ninth President of the African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6513.speech: Has outlined four strategic pillars to guide his work and position the AfDB as a top provider of development finance for the continent: unlocking Africa's financial resources, reforming and consolidating Africa's financial sovereignty, turning demographics into a dividend, and building resilient infrastructure ; has also committed to working closely with donor countries to ensure a successful replenishment of the African Development Fund (ADF), the bank's primary funding source for low-income countries in Africa.

a6513.speaker: 2025 African Economic Outlook report
a6513.speech: According to the report, the continent's growth is projected to increase from 3.3% in 2024 to 3.9% in 2025. The report also notes that 21 African countries are expected to see growth of more than 5% in 2025.

a6543.speaker: Unicef, the UN children’s agency (report)
a6543.speech: Says armed men are raping and sexually assaulting children as young as one during Sudan’s civil war; says that, although 221 rape cases against children have been officially reported since the start of 2024, the true number is likely to be much higher; reports that a third of the victims were boys, who typically face “unique challenges” in reporting such crimes and seeking the help they need, and that 16 of the victims were under the age of five years, including four infants; does not say who is responsible.

a6543.speaker: Other UN investigations
a6543.speech: Have blamed the majority of rapes on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), saying RSF fighters had a pattern of using sexual violence to terrorise civilians and suppress opposition to their advances.

a6543.speaker: Mohamed Chande Othman, chair of the UN’s fact-finding mission
a6543.speech: “The sheer scale of sexual violence we have documented in Sudan is staggering.”

a6543.speaker: International human rights groups (evidence presented)
a6543.speech: According to evidence presented, victims in the RSF’s stronghold of Darfur were often targeted because they were black African rather than Arab, apparently with the aim of driving them out of Sudan.

a6543.speaker: Omnia (not her real name), adult female survivor held by armed men
a6543.speech: “After nine at night, someone opens the door, carrying a whip, selects one of the girls, and takes her to another room. I could hear the little girl crying and screaming. They were raping her” ; “Every time they raped her, this girl would come back covered in blood. She is still just a young child. They only release these girls at dawn, and they return almost unconscious. Each of them cries and speaks incoherently. During the 19 days I spent there, I reached a point where I wanted to end my life.”

a6543.speaker: The UN
a6543.speech: Says three out of four school-age girls are out of school.

a6543.speaker: Sudanese coordinating committee that monitors the Emergency Response Rooms
a6543.speech: Said the activists relied quite heavily on US aid, and most have been forced to shut down.

a6543.speaker: UN organization dedicated to protecting women’s rights
a6543.speech: Says local organisations led by women are vital in delivering support to survivors of sexual violence, but they receive less than 2% of the total funding of the UN’s Sudan Humanitarian Fund.

a6543.speaker: Sulaima Elkhalifa, Sudanese human rights defender who runs a government unit on combatting violence against women
a6543.speech: Said the local group known as “She Leads” was not a big expense, measured in the tens of thousands of dollars, but enabled case workers to reach around 35 survivors a month; told the BBC that those who have been raped by armed men “don’t have the luxury of being depressed”, adding that the demands of war – finding food, needing to flee – leave no space to deal with trauma.

a6601.speaker: Participants at the 2nd Edition of the African Conference on Agricultural Technologies (ACAT 2025 Joint Communiqué)
a6601.speech: Welcomed the resolutions of the Ministerial dialogue; called for the scaling of participatory and adaptive farmer extension, education and training models; committed to prioritize the needs of women and youthful farmers and agripreneurs; encouraged African governments, regional economic communities, continental bodies and organs to heighten efforts towards mechanisms for derisking agriculture, increased investments, public-private partnerships, cross-continental and intercontinental collaboration and building necessary rural infrastructure for sustainable Ag-Tech commercialization; recognized the youth as a strong force driving the development and adoption of Ag-tech in Africa; committed to exploring transparent frameworks for respectful and fair integration of traditional technical knowledge into formal research and development systems; noted that intellectual property protection, when managed ethically and equitably, is an enabler and not a hindrance to innovation; encouraged the promotion of inclusive, open-source licensing models for plant materials; reiterated that no single entity can drive sustainable agricultural transformation in Africa; recommitted to sustain engagement on agricultural technology between ACAT editions through Strategic Dialogues on Agricultural Technologies (SDATA); endorsed the recognition and adoption of ACAT as the continent-wide biennial forum; and resolved to meet again in Nairobi, Kenya in May 2027 to take stock of progress.

a6601.speaker: Ministerial dialogue chaired by Hon. Dr. Mark Cyubahiro Bagabe, Minister for Agriculture and Animal Resources, Republic of Rwanda (resolutions)
a6601.speech: Emphasised enhanced public budget allocations towards ag-tech related rural infrastructure development and agricultural training at public universities; catalyzing and fostering multi-sectoral collaboration to drive participatory and co-creation initiatives between the public sector, research institutions, civil society, the private sector and farming communities; advancing regional harmonization and alignment of national aspirations with continental blueprints and creating an enabling environment to drive Ag-Tech commercialization; and ensuring equitable access to agro-inputs and climate-smart innovations, adequate extension, and long-term food security and mainstreaming the youth, women, and rural farmers in Government policies and strategies.

a6601.speaker: Participants at ACAT 2025 (closing of the Joint Communiqué)
a6601.speech: “We recognize and appreciate the commitment of the former President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and AATF Goodwill Ambassador for Agricultural Technologies, His Excellency Dr. Goodluck Jonathan” and “fully appreciate His Excellency President Paul Kagame and the people of Rwanda for their hospitality and hosting of ACAT 2025 edition.”

a6699.speaker: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief) (announcement at international donors' conference)
a6699.speech: The announcement of Saudi humanitarian aid for Mali was made at the conclusion of a conference of international donors to support refugees in the Sahel and Lake Chad regions, held recently in Saudi Arabia; Mali is among the beneficiaries of a fund of more than 1.1 billion dollars mobilised by KSrelief, an initiative supported by the OIC, OCHA and UNHCR, aiming to provide essential support to displaced populations in Mali and neighbouring countries.

a6699.speaker: Recent United Nations reports
a6699.speech: Confirmed the figure that in 2024 approximately 7.1 million people in Mali need humanitarian aid, nearly 30% of the population.

a6699.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a6699.speech: At a recent donors' conference held in Saudi Arabia, reiterated the importance of increased international aid for the populations of the Sahel, whose development potential is immense despite the current challenges.

a6984.speaker: UNHCR (UN refugee agency)
a6984.speech: Confirmed that four refugees and a local government official had been injured when police intervened to stop the protesters at the Kakuma refugee camp on Monday ; said in a statement that it was "deeply concerned" about the impact of the cuts, and that "government security personnel in Kakuma intervened to contain the situation. Fortunately, there was no loss of life. However, at least four refugees and one local government official sustained injuries. UNHCR cannot confirm the use of live rounds during the demonstrations."

a6984.speaker: Andrew Dafir, refugee in Kakuma camp
a6984.speech: Having received a text telling him his monthly ration would drop from 4kg to 3kg of cereals, while cooking oil and beans had been cut completely, said: "I feel neglected and lost because I have no other way to survive" ; said what they had been receiving was already very limited after repeated cuts, with the full ration being more than 7kg a month for each person ; said the total cash payment covered barely enough food for a day, let alone for a month, and that the new level of food aid was not enough to live on, especially for those who did not have any other income to supplement their rations.

a6984.speaker: Andrew Dafir, refugee in Kakuma camp
a6984.speech: Shared a video of scores of people running away from teargas and what sounded like bullets being fired, with a boy being carried away with an injury to his stomach, and said one of his friends was among those hurt ; "I lost my voice, I was so scared" ; "We're being forced to be silent; it seems like no wants to listen to us."

a6984.speaker: Youth Voices in Kakuma (group of young refugees based in the camp)
a6984.speech: Said protesters had spent hours outside the UNHCR offices but when no one came out to listen to their concerns some began trying to climb the fence, prompting the police to step in.

a6984.speaker: Blax Von, Kakuma resident who uploaded videos of the protest on to TikTok
a6984.speech: Said the tensions had been building for several months, with water supplies being reduced, cash support payments slashed, and refugees required to pay their children's school fees.

a6984.speaker: A South Sudanese refugee (unnamed), holding an empty cooking pot, speaking to the Associated Press
a6984.speech: "This is the container they are now using to measure beans and oil and the other one for rice. And this is equivalent for one month for your food" ; "Assume you don't have another income, it's only this. Is this enough for you?"

a6984.speaker: The Social Justice Centre Working Group, a Kenyan civil society organisation
a6984.speech: "Brutalising those who flee war, persecution and hunger instead of addressing their cries for food and water is the height of state-sponsored cruelty."

a6984.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen, cabinet secretary at Kenya's interior ministry
a6984.speech: Said on Tuesday that the recent aid cuts had had a "sudden and severe" impact on Kenya's ability to host 800,000 refugees and asylum seekers: "With the cut in funding for humanitarian assistance programmes by the developed world, the socioeconomic impact on our country will be unbearable. And yet to turn our backs on the most vulnerable people runs counter to our belief in shared humanity. It's therefore incumbent on developed countries to shoulder the financial burden as we do our bit."

a7017.speaker: Mirriam Sabi, Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) Director Innovation and Project Management
a7017.speech: Said the symposium was also meant to making it easier for SMEs to comply by providing them with knowledge needed so that they contributed to domestic tax revenue ; “SMEs are the lifeblood of our economy, driving innovation, creating jobs, and fostering economic growth and so they fuel progress and prosperity in our nation. We gather here today to educate them fully on what they are required to do with regards to tax compliance and we shall touch on all tax compliance matters especially on obligations. The goal is clear, we want to empower SMEs with tax knowledge so that they can comply with tax matters with ease.”

a7017.speaker: Edward Koos, USAID Revenue for Growth Project Chief of Party
a7017.speech: Committed to continue supporting efforts that would enhance tax compliance; announced that there were a number of tax grants available meant to raise awareness on tax related matters; believed that open dialogue was critical to the creation of an enabling environment that all businesses, including MSMEs would be tax compliant ; “To support private public dialogue and tax awareness, USAID has a number of activities. We are planning to support the upcoming budget symposium. We have also been providing media trainings with ZRA on tax issues where we enhance the ability of media to understand and report on tax issues.”

a7017.speaker: Ngande Manajiti, Lusaka District Business Association Chairperson
a7017.speech: Stressed the importance of paying taxes, saying no country had developed without them.

a7153.speaker: Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA)
a7153.speech: Has announced a half billion dollar catalytic fund to back efforts to improve food security on the continent over the next five years; the organisation looks to reach 28 million farmers across 15 countries to boost productivity and income.

a7153.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a7153.speech: Estimate that 22 million people in the region are already in the clutches of a growing food crisis.

a7153.speaker: Experts
a7153.speech: Forecast that the coming months will bring the region's fifth consecutive failed rainy season, exacerbating the crisis.

a7153.speaker: UN officials
a7153.speech: Warn that more than 200,000 are at risk of dying — potentially by the end of the year – if action is not taken immediately.

a7161.speaker: Scott Perry (Pennsylvania), member of the U.S. House of Representatives
a7161.speech: Accused the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) of financing terrorist organizations. According to him, USAID spent $697 million annually, not counting cash transfers, to support terrorist groups such as ISIS, ISIS-K and their training camps. These accusations were made during the hearings of the Committee on Public Administration Efficiency (DOGE), held on February 13.

a7167.speaker: Rema, Nigerian musician
a7167.speech: Said he knew the song would do well and thanked Selena for taking part in the work ; “I believe that everything I do is special, different songs will resonate with different people; when I went into the studio I was truly singing my truth, I did what I had to do,” said Rema in an interview with People.

a7373.speaker: British Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC), leading 13 NGOs operating in South Sudan
a7373.speech: Stated on Thursday: "If the conflict in South Sudan continues, and aid does not increase, then it is likely that by August localised areas of South Sudan will sink into famine."

a7373.speaker: Head of the Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC), the group of humanitarian organisations
a7373.speech: Said the risk of famine is very real in certain regions and that "millions of people are facing an extreme food crisis".

a7430.speaker: United Nations and its humanitarian agencies
a7430.speech: Are sounding the alarm over the escalation of violence, which would include a war crime; all fear having to manage a prolonged conflict that would affect the whole Horn of Africa ; the UN is unable to bring assistance to more than two million people in need of humanitarian aid in the region, including half a million people in a situation of food insecurity, plus 200,000 internally displaced people and more than 100,000 refugees from Eritrea, all based in Tigray ; the UN is very worried that the conflict will continue to escalate because nearly 9 million people could suffer its consequences.

a7430.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a7430.speech: Is very concerned by the situation because 14,500 Ethiopians, 50% of them children, have already crossed the border to take shelter in neighbouring Sudan, whose absorption capacity is very limited.

a7430.speaker: Michelle Bachelet, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
a7430.speech: Shared her very grave concern about the alarming deterioration of the situation in the Tigray region; warned the Ethiopian authorities and the leaders of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) about the continuation of hostilities, which could become uncontrollable, cause destruction and lead to massive displacement inside the country and beyond its borders.

a7430.speaker: Amnesty International (NGO)
a7430.speech: According to Amnesty International, hundreds of people were killed with knives and machetes on the night of 9 November in the town of Mai-Kadra, in south-western Tigray.

a7430.speaker: Eyewitnesses
a7430.speech: Stated that TPLF supporters were responsible for the massacre.

a7430.speaker: Michelle Bachelet, UN human rights chief
a7430.speech: Declared that if the facts were confirmed, they would constitute a war crime; she calls for the establishment of an independent investigation.

a7430.speaker: Numerous experts
a7430.speech: Fear that a civil war could set the country ablaze, where the 9 different regions are already fighting to obtain more autonomy or threatening to secede.

a7430.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a7430.speech: Said he was “deeply alarmed by the situation” in Tigray, stressing that “the stability of Ethiopia is important for the whole Horn of Africa”.

a7490.speaker: Commander of US AFRICOM
a7490.speech: Accused Captain Ibrahim Traore, in substance, of using Burkina Faso’s gold for personal ends.
